Results of Operator Chen Qianyu's background checks are not complicated. The operator is as consistent, simple, and straightforward as she appears. 
Operator Chen Qianyu grew up in the Hongshan Crater and studied swordmancy at Tanjian Hall. Prior to joining Endfield, she has interned at various organizations and served different individual employers. Hence, in spite of her young age, Operator Chen has years of solo combat experiences. After a period of adjustment, she has now grown used to team-based combat. 
Unlike many youths who lost their parents in pioneering operations in the unforgiving and disaster-ridden lands of Talos-II, Chen Qianyu grew up in a wholesome and happy family. Her relatively simple childhood also gave her unshakable optimism. She is often praised for her excellent teamwork and sunny personality in multiple instances of team-based operations. Many key collaborators, including Chief Engineer Andre, have high hopes for Operator Chen and believe that she is a poster child for a certain facet of Endfield: Young, positive, friendly, and eager to intercede and solve any problem that needs to be solved. 

[ADDITIONAL NOTES] 
During early contact, we realized that Operator Chen Qianyu has, without question or doubt, earned stellar performance reviews at multiple employers. However, many are still curious why she never stayed at any particular employer for extended periods of time. To date, Operator Chen has spent the longest period of time working for Endfield. We asked her this question during a regular interview and her answers are provided below: 
"Cheers and Drinks at La Fantoma? Wait, did I actually work there for three months?! Yeah, that's easy to explain. I had my fill of the milk tea so I left." 
"Oh... Temporary security personnel. Yeah, I wasn't old enough to get an actual job but I really needed the money for my next stop. My only choice was to work in EXPOs and conferences. But yeah, those were the months when I met plenty of big shots in Talos-II..." 
"Hold on! My graduation year performance at Tanjian Hall is actually — EXCELLENT?! Wait! You're not reading it wrong, right? I ... well, it's normal for me to be clueless about this! Heheh! I never picked up enough courage to check the results... Yeah, I'm just a little worried that my mentors would compare me to my mom." 
"I spent more than a year in Yinglung Special Task Force... Yeah, I did that, but can we not talk about this? Well, there's nothing to hide. I just don't find the place a good match for me. Wha? Did you just say there are people who don't get along with me?! Okay, that's ridiculous! Know anything about Duccio the Half-Face? That notorious gang leader at the Asphalt Roundabout? I actually had a pretty nice convo with him, you know!"

A massive Landbreaker army had encircled a wildlands village. The breakers prepared themselves for a full scale assault. Hopelessness spread like a plague amongst the garrisoned Endfield operators and the local residents. 
That was the moment when they saw her. Arclight of the Hannabit Circuit — the lone Songseeker who roared into the town astride her motorcycle. 
She tore through the rear of the breaker army and seized control of the situation without hesitation. Under her leadership, the residents created a defense line with their wagons and salvage. The elderly and children were moved to the hills. Everyone who could work dug the trenches and set up simple Originium defense units. Every action was calm and simple, and she moved throughout the place like a part of the wildlands itself. 
On the eve of the Landbreaker attack, thunder rumbled from afar. The monsoons came as usual, and a nightlong of torrential rain carved a new creek that coursed through the place. Arclight may have memorized every corner of the wildlands. The river coursed through the trenches that Arclight directed and became a protective moat that protected the entire village. The flood waters also washed through the breakers' camp and foiled their attack formations. 
The Landbreakers did not leave empty handed. They attempted to ford the moat and assail the defenses, but every attack was beaten back by Arclight, the Endfielders, and village residents. In the end, the raiders were forced to escape under the cover of a rainy night. 
When the dark rainclouds finally left the wildlands, Arclight found the Endfield operator who was sending a report to Dijiang. She waved a letter of recommendation to the skies and said, "The quaking of the wildlands dirt led me here. Now, please lead me to Endfield."

The hinge of the courtyard gate had broken down for a while. It probably broke two weeks after Chen Chichi left. When Guang Jianshan noticed the hinge broken in two, he couldn't help but feel he had already seen this coming. Every time someone pushed open the gate to enter or leave the garden, the hinge would release an irksome groan loud enough to be heard in the house. Even the study. The groan at five during sunrise was Chen heading out to practice swordmancy. The groan at eight in the morning was Chen rushing back home, picking up her school bag, grabbing the food from her father's plate, taking two messy bites out of it, and rushing out to Tanjian Hall for her classes. The groan at five in the afternoon was Chen running back into the courtyard while chasing fowlbeasts through the grove, humming a song, and swishing a well-balanced stick around. The groan at midnight was Chen secretly jumping out of her second floor bedroom. She thought her father would not know how she sneaked off to have fun on her own. 
Jianshan knew everything. He had quietly paved a flat path leading to the gate and got rid of the protruding stones. He would not want his careless darling girl to trip and fall in the darkness. 
He had always been a dutiful father who acted rather than lectured. His name, Jianshan, meant "builder of Hongshan". When Chichi first learned about his actual name, she laughed and said that it was too down-to-earth, like a hard and stubborn stone. The stone was the ballast that secured their life in the Hongshan Crater. The stone restrained its ability to skip across rivers and lakes, and sank itself into cities and civilization. The stone stayed behind, even after she left, and allowed itself to be covered in moss. 
And today the gate groaned again. Jianshan leaped up from his desk and went straight to the living room. His daughter kicked off her shoes, threw down her traveling satchel, and collapsed into the sofa. None of it felt normal. Jianshan counted the days in his mind. She stayed for three days during the new year holidays and had not been back for six months afterwards. Her return to Hongshan in an ordinary Monday afternoon was strange. Her credit card reported no expenses for nearly four days. How did she survive? And why did she look so tired and exhausted? Did she take the wrong bus? Hongshan Crater was known for its complex geography and people who seldom returned often messed up the rides and had to walk long detours to be home — But Jianshan kept all these questions to himself. 
"Hungry?" 
His darling girl nodded. 
He made some noodles and added two extra pieces of meat. The young lass was still growing. 
Qianyu came to the kitchen and served the table. She did not forget Chichi's rules despite romping through the world for fourteen months. They sat facing each other and had their meals. 
"What experiments have you been running, Dad?" 
"You probably won't know much about it." 
"Well, it'd be great if you cook as well as you do science. Your tests got all those generous HAS grants." 
"Your mom likes what I make." 
"Does that mean Mom had no taste? This is really salty." 
No matter the conversation, she would typically finish everything, even the soup. But this day was different. She set her chopsticks aside after two bites, and just sat on the chair as her eyes gazed outside. 
"Dad, I think I have trouble staying at a single place for long." 
He knew that Chen was clear that he could not and would not say anything, and probably did not know how to continue this topic. He usually just let the discussion slide. But her drooping tail and expressions looked particularly sad on this day. He suddenly realized that his prodigal daughter had matured somewhat, and was slowly learning her lessons. 
"Coals on your feet?" Guang Jianshan asked, "Your old man used to be a pretty fast runner. I can't afford to be slow, or your mama's blade would catch up to me." 
"What are you talking about?" 
"I used to hike the mountains carrying a hundred kilos of surveillance gear. You've seen them before. Big telescopes? It's always down to the training. The old Tianshi would fly around and lead the way while we ran along the foot of the mountains and tried to keep up..." 
"Ugh. Stop it already...! Hooo. I don't think I can find a place that fits me." 
She raised her head. The resemblance hit him and left him a little dazed. 
"Well, your ma... She actually left Hongshan three times. And that's just counting this place." 
"What? Why didn't you tell about this?!" 
"Because you probably won't understand." 
Jianshan saw the glimmer and spark return to his daughter's face. Chen was back, and quickly enough. 
"When did all this happen? Before I was born? Or when you moved back to Hongshan? Was that the last time she left? You told me she went to that Rho..." 
"Push me all you want. Your mama told me to keep it from you." 
"Ahhhhh! That silly old woman! Why?!" 
He looked at the girl who started eating her noodles once more. 
"So when are you moving out again?"

Having an operator like Typhoeus, who excels at wilderness survival, join us has made our work in the north go much more smoothly.
Although Endfield works closely with the Order of Steel Oath, they are often too occupied with their own battles to spare much time for us. More often than not, they lead us to the site of a rift, then must return to the front lines, leaving the rest of the work to us.
The polar environment is harsh, with year-round snow cover and extremely low temperatures, creating many difficulties for our monitoring work. A sudden blizzard destroyed our camp and knocked out all our instruments. In despair, we wrapped ourselves in every blanket we had, waiting to be consumed by the frozen wasteland. Fortunately, Operator Typhoeus arrived just in time.
Along with her came an entire animal leg.
In the ruins, Typhoeus lit a campfire and brought warmth with a Sami-style barbecue. She then ventured alone into the blizzard, returning with wood and bark, and in just one afternoon, built a log cabin large enough for four people using nothing but primitive materials.
Though she knew nothing about the facilities we brought, she was still able to set up a stable environment for them to run properly according to our needs. When we faced the rifts head-on, she efficiently cleared away the attacking swarms of Aggeloi using her hunting experience, assisting us in placing the equipment and retrieving critical data.
Aside from her outdoors survival skills, what everyone trusted most was her remarkably accurate intuition.
Yes, relying on a colleague's intuition for work does not sound like something a professional would say. But when all our navigation facilities were down, her instincts were what allowed us to narrowly dodge danger and evacuate safely. Throughout the journey, we were constantly on edge, yet she never showed a hint of fear, always calmly pointing the way through the snowstorm for everyone.
Some speculate that it was the Cyclops living in the mountains who taught Typhoeus how to see the future. But I believe that this is simply the way the Sami people coexist with nature. By placing themselves within it and becoming part of it, they can keenly perceive nature's breath, its pulse, its heartbeat, and in doing so, receive the revelations that nature bestows.

Endministrator and Supervisor Perlica of Endfield Industries: 
I am extremely pleased to learn that Laevatain has returned with the Endministrator's help. Though her journey is far from complete, her return proves that she has found a new objective and people whom she is willing to travel with. 
Extremely powerful "desire and hope" drove Laevatain to step onto the lands of Talos-II. When we first sensed her existence, the light she gave off was bedazzling. I later realized that this light was emitted by her obsession — her innermost ego demanding the answer: "Who am I?" 
Led on by the said obsession, the fragments awakened and created a complete persona. "She" walked out of the Originium Woods, new and intact, and arrived at Rhodes Island bearing the name "Laevatain". I thought she would immediately become one of our strongest assets and supporters, but she turned us down. Just like Surtr who had always walked alone, no one can command Laevatain or force her to stay in one place. She will answer to no faction until she finds the answer to dispel her own miasma of amnesia. Hence, we decided to open the doors and give her our best farewells. 
Once, I was worried that Laevatain's choice would affect other reconveners. Then I realized that they became reconveners because every one of them did not forget the old dream and vision. And that is why they reconvened with you on this very same path. Now, this thought alone has lifted a stone off my chest. 
Since Laevatain is currently an official Endfielder fighting along your side, then allow me to share a few words of advice (based on my knowledge of "her") for "getting along with her". 
Firstly, accommodate and accept Laevatain's straightforward nature. She often says whatever that comes to her mind. It is not an act of hostility, malice, or rudeness. In fact, such words are a symbol of her sincere and undisguised attitude — "I prefer to simply tell you what I'm thinking right now." 
Secondly, should Laevatain exhibit obvious signs of fury or impatience, do not attempt to persuade her to "calm" down. Believe me, there are more effective means, such as the provision of ice cream or other things that can rapidly "cool" the situation. Laevatain is someone you can communicate with, but she dislikes "being told what to do". 
Just as a side note, before she left Rhodes Island, she took all the crimsonberry ice cream from my lab freezer — and ate them all, right before my eyes, as though it was the right thing to do. "Thought you told me memories can lie," she said as she licked the spoon, "So I better have more of this to make it as memorable as possible." Laevatain marked her farewell with this action to ensure the veracity of the moment. She actually cares very deeply about her friends, far more deeply than most would like to think. 
Thirdly, Laevatain is extremely similar to Surtr, but according to her temperament... Do not tell her that she resembles Surtr. Also, do not tell her that she DOES NOT resemble Surtr. In fact, do not ever compare her to Surtr, unless she brings the topic up herself. Always remember this! 
Best wishes in your collective journey across Talos-II. 

Rhodes Island

Mr. Dolly's Game III 
Gazing out at the glistening coastline and distant skyscrapers, a long-forgotten name came to Ardelia's mind — Siesta, a volcanic city wrapped in warm memories. 
But, this was La Fantoma — the gem of Band, the gilded city of Talos-II. 
As a renowned geologist, Ardelia was invited to speak at a major academic forum on "Order in the New Geological Ecology of Talos-II." She had only planned to deliver a standard presentation, but to her surprise, her speech caused quite a stir. 
Corporate representatives quickly surrounded her, sharing blueprints for a new industrial park and asking for her thoughts. Senior researchers eagerly shared their latest findings, hoping to spark potential collaborations with Ardelia. Even government officials brought thick binders and invited her to join their next major project. 
Just like that, a quiet field researcher had become the star of the show. 
What began as simple handshakes soon turned into warm compliments — "You're an inspiration to us all." In the elevator, someone stopped Ardelia with a notebook, asking for an autograph to hang in his lab. At crosswalks, kids would shout, "I wanna be a scientist too!" Even a street vendor handed her a soda, saying, "My nephew loves geology — got any book recommendations?" 
At first, Ardelia found it moving. She nodded politely to every earnest face, patiently answered each well-meaning question. But slowly, exhaustion crept in. She didn't resent these people, nor did she dislike their attention. It was just… she wasn't ready to be "known". 
After a grueling three-hour roundtable, she pushed open the door and ran. She passed a giant poster of herself labeled "Young Female Scientist Role Model" and vanished into the crowd. 
That's when she realized: Mr. Dolly was gone. 
No one knew what it was or where it had gone. In a shopping mall, a woman screamed about "something fluffy" bumping into her. On a rooftop, a flower bed was trampled flat by "something pink." Someone even posted a blurry photo "something round" darting over the ticket gate — carrying a bag of cotton candy. 
Ardelia tracked these clues and searched half of the city. Her shoes wore thin, mud clung to her skirt, and headache crept over her. 
Nearly out of breath, she stumbled out of a side alley and stopped. 
It was a patch of untouched wilderness at the city's edge — untamed, bursting with wildflowers. The sea breeze carried their fragrance in gentle waves. And there, lay Mr. Dolly, sprawled at the heart of it all, motionless as the earth itself. 
"What are you even doing here?" Ardelia asked, half-frustrated, half-amused. Mr. Dolly didn't answer. He just rolled over lazily. 
Ardelia walked over and sat beside him. Then, she switched off her handyterm. The meetings, the obligations — all of it could wait. 
After all, nothing suits a geologist better than the open wild.

I still remember the first time I met Ekut. The patrolling Huntsingers brought her back to the camp and the girl was barely alive. It was difficult for us to fathom why such a young child was left to roam the wildlands for months on her own, a suffering that almost killed her with malnutrition and thirst. To treat the injuries on her right arm, we were forced to reconnect the nerves with circuitry. Of course, there is no need to be worried about the hazards posed by her right hand. We have designed a special pair of insulation gloves so that she may live normally like us. 
I named her Ekut, based on the strong and intelligent burdenbeast of our hanna. It is my hope that she could grow up strong, and survive the wind and frost like the powerful burdenbeast. She achieved all that, and went beyond my expectations. 
But Ekut grew up with an immense duty that seemed far too heavy for her. Perhaps it was her early victory over death itself, or her powerful name we took from the hanna. When she turned fifteen, Ekut started to seek the songs and roamed the wildlands. The Songseeker did everything she could to help villages and towns in dire straits, even when the challenges were far too great. 
I still remember that rainstorm. During our rescue operation, Ekut ventured alone into the heart of the tempest. We thought she would never come back. Just when all hopes seemed lost, an arc of lightning streaked across the sky. Like that arc, she pierced the fury of nature and leaped onto the last wagon. And with this act, the wildlands began to address her as Arclight. The name was woven into the hanna of numerous Songseekers. She took a name from the verses and returned a new name to their songs. 
I was not surprised when Arclight told me that she wanted to seek new answers from Endfield. In fact, it reminded me of the choice I made when I was younger. I once roamed far to the canopies of starry night, and from there I felt a chorus of hope and courage assembled in the floating city. 
Those memories felt like they belonged to a lifetime ago. But I believe that as long as the stars still shine in the sky, Civilization will one day be united once more. I also believe that Arclight, along with the names and oaths she wove into her hanna, will find the answers she truly seeks. 
— Letter of Recommendation for Endfield Industries, written by Aldertone Orisha

Operator Yvonne was recommended by Crowe of UWST to Andre. She joined the Specialist Tech Division of Endfield Industries via the "Specialized Talent Recruitment" channel. Yvonne is now leading several research projects on the Æther, the Blight, and the Trans-Æther Tranquilizer-Automata associated with the previous two. Given her outstanding scientific research capabilities, she has received bonus grants and resources to support her independent research. 

During background checks, many have described Yvonne as an engineer with an obvious streak of "rebellion". However, I cannot be more opposed to this evaluation. And no, this has nothing to do with the laser stickers she adhered upon my chassis. 
In my opinion, the core issue rests in the inability of most individuals to keep up with her rapid train of thought. The end result would appear that she has teamwork issues. Also, she is rather confident in her personal style that she constructed for herself after years of scientific research... Her violations were never deliberate. Instead, they should be considered instinctive reactions when someone or something attempts to interfere with her way of thinking or self-expression. 
Such personality quirks withstood the influences of the environment and many would often regard this as Yvonne's rebel spirit. However, her brightly colored outfits, carefree graffiti, and complex yet extremely practical chassis designs are modes of expression that she has consistently maintained — in a world filled with rules and boundaries, those who remain true to themselves would seem rather out of place. Fortunately, Endfield is not a place dictated by inflexible regulations. Our vision is to change this world, instead of sustaining its current existence by sticking to the law. 
Moreover, when our people described Yvonne as a "rebel", they did so with a smile. 
— Martin Marvin Malen, Assistant, HR Division, Endfield Industries

DOCUMENT: A private letter 
Lamp: 
Where are you, darling babe? Your great granny, grand aunt, aunt, and sister heard (from me) that you quit your job and left home. They've got a ton of questions, and they are relentless. Even the best-fabricated story would breach under their endless drilling. Anyway, the family exploded when they learned you really left home, just as we expected. Looking on the bright side, I kept it a secret for 3 weeks. But Mama's gotta know where you've been all this time. 
I know our argument at Arlirye left quite a bad taste in the mouth. Mama still doesn't support your choice but when I got back home and sat down, I suddenly remembered that trip I had planned when I was a young gal like you. My bag was already packed and leaning right against the wall. I was that close to picking it up and marching through the door to get somewhere far away when I heard you. You were in your baby feeding chair and smiling at me with a baby knife and fork in your hands. And I stayed. I'm sharing this story with you because I wish to tell you that your hope of leaving home might be an inherited habit. 
Though your great granny likes to talk about it, the scenes that our pioneering ancestors witnessed after crossing the Cosmic Gate had already faded away into patches of mold on the wall. They were part of the gigantic convoy column, a great wall of vehicles that stretched all the way to the edge of the horizon. The truckers kept driving, up till the very eve of Severance. That was how we found our first pot of gold, the starting capital upon which we built our logistics business in Alloycarrot. However, as we spent longer and longer time chasing after mineral veins, our kin no longer felt at home when placed behind the wheel. 
Watch out for enemies on the road. Your TGCC job wasn't exactly low profile and we had a share of visitors. Rest assured, no one's going to hurt my darling baby doll. 
I'll handle the rest of our family for you. Don't forget to send us pictures from your traveling. 

Mama 

DOCUMENT: A private letter 
Mama: 
Finding network connection in the wildlands is no easy task. But a solo journey is everything I dreamed of. Sweet and beautiful. 
I stopped by New Wrankwood right after leaving home. They tried to recreate the scene to heal trauma, but it ended up quite disappointing, since no one was interested in the horror genre. And the place just wouldn't stop raining. I didn't like it. 
The Northern Corridor is my next destination, and I'll soon be reaching the edge of the Band. Just yesterday, a painter at the motel told me about the breathtaking natural landscapes waiting for me once I leave the Band cities. I intend to explore the old frontiers of the north. People say there are ruins that date back before the collapse of the Cosmic Gate. They're the things that great granny kept talking about, right? Don't worry about me getting into dangerous situations. I've been traveling with a group of Hannabit Circuit Songseekers. Once I find decent connection, I'll send you photos of me riding a burdenbeast. 
FYI, someone just piqued my interest. Whenever I found a place to rest my legs and talk to the locals, I would hear a name called the "Endministrator". Coincidentally, my itinerary basically matched this "Endministrator's" northward expedition. Is it possible that I've found my match in Talos-II in the field of professional traveling? 

Lamp

While serving as a messenger in our Specialist Tech Division, Operator Avywenna could not give a more different vibe than Operator Gilberta. The latter is known throughout Endfield for her uninhibited sweetness and geniality. Avywenna, on the other hand, approaches socializing like a professional and manages relationships accordingly. 
One has to work with Operator Avywenna for extended periods of time before noticing her peculiar quirks. For example, despite being extremely loquacious during small gatherings or in private, everyone who recalled the exchanges would realize that they hardly got any truth from Avywenna — especially about herself. Nevertheless, people tend to find themselves spilling their beans with Avywenna as she proved to be an excellent listener. She is always capable of asking friendly questions, leading on discussions along the direction she has planned, and concluding dialogs at just the perfect moments. 
Avywenna personally explained such skills with her background. She was born to a huge Cautus family living in the Free City of Alloycarrot. Patience easily becomes the most important virtue when living with a huge number of kin. This claim has been verified. Querying "Avywenna" in the population database of Alloycarrot gives you over 80 individuals with the same name. 
Whenever Avywenna casually drops a morsel of info about herself, it's always a subtle bait to get her conversational partner to lay everything out. A short dialog is all she needs to acquire background information and contacts about everyone she is chatting with. Avywenna would also argue, with great cunning, that she did so out of professional habit that carried over from her messenger career, where one must constantly deal with people. 
One thing to note: no one resents Avywenna's air of mystery. Instead, it only got more people interested in chatting her up. Her presence has greatly enhanced Endfield's ability to navigate the local affairs that are often tangled and delicate. Avywenna is a master at resolving conflicts and diffusing tension, walking away without a scratch. She is like a miner navigating the criss-crossing mines and tunnels of Alloycarrot. The one directing the situation will never feel lost.

Mr. Dolly's Game I 
Shortly after joining Endfield, Ardelia visited a Blight-ravaged sector of Talos-II. The geological disaster had shredded a once-peaceful settlement, leaving fissures that pulsed with residual energy. Survivors bore wounds beyond the physical, their eyes hollow with the kind of trauma only disaster refugees know. 
Ardelia stayed at the shelter for a while. The wounded crowded steel cots — limbs lost, eyes vacant, voices severed by trauma. White curtains divided their suffering as medical monitors pulsed like weary hearts. 
Ardelia worked tirelessly — organizing supplies, changing bandages, murmuring "I understand your sorrow" to the wounded. Until a voice, serrated with grief, cut through: "You don't understand." 
It was a young girl. Small but fierce, she forced the words through gritted teeth: "You stand straight. Your steps don't falter. No disaster has carved its marks into you." 
The girl turned away, her voice fraying at the edges. "Stop. Just stop pretending. Maybe you've been sick, but you healed. That's luck we'll never taste. Our stories end in the same sentence: lifelong pain. So when you say you 'understand'... is that pity's cheap coin? Spare us." 
Ardelia stood there in her research coat, ponytail precise, steps steady, and eyes bright. The Originium had scoured the reconvener's illness away, attuning her to wind whispers and microscopic fractures in stone. Yet here, before those still drowning in pain, her engineered perfection rendered her mute. 
When darkness fell upon the land, Mr. Dolly appeared. 
It trotted between beds and corridors, leaving chaos in its wake — toppling medicine cabinets, upending tea trays, kicking a freshly filled hot-water bottle beneath pillows. Nurses cursed the sudden swelter; children shrieked about 'something furry' burrowing under their blankets. 
Ardelia chased Mr. Dolly into an old break room where she tugged at a canvas sheet to reveal a dust-choked piano. It stomped the keys, a discordant chime that jolted Ardelia into clarity. 
Ardelia approached, brushing away the dust. The yellowed keys stared back, a few bass notes dissonant but functional. She sat, fingertips tracing a tentative sequence of Leithanian arpeggios into the stale air. 
First piece ... second ... and as the third began, soft footsteps whispered from the hallway's depths. 
Mr. Dolly lay curled nearby, a silent cushion of warmth. The children nestled against its fur, their breaths syncing with Ardelia's piano as the notes wove through the stale air. 
The young girl came in as well, perching quietly in the farthest corner. 
"It still hurts," she murmured, "but when you play... the world becomes something worth enduring."

Everyone called her "Younger Dame" at Qingbo Stockade because Ruan Lin had only one child of his own, and later plucked another out of the water. The first was named "One (Yi)," so the second naturally became "Younger". The folks of Qingbo Stockade always thought in simple, straightforward ways.
No one knew where Younger Dame came from. Ruan Yi said she was a kitten in a bamboo basket that he picked up. Ruan Lin said she was a treasure, the River's Daughter sent by the Ancestral Spring. A young boy nearby, hearing this, asked, if Younger Dame was born of the river, didn't that make her the river's master?! Upon hearing this, Tangtang puffed out her chest, leaped onto her bamboo hobbyhorse, and declared proudly: "Exactly! The water is mine! Qingbo Stockade is mine! All the good food and fun are mine too!"
Ruan Lin ruffled her hair and burst into hearty laughter. Soon, everyone gathered around the fire joined in, their mirth contagious enough to make Tangtang giggle along. The conversation drifted to other things, and the matter was never brought up again.
It wasn't until Tangtang grew a little older that one day, as she listened to the Stockaders talking, a thought suddenly struck her. River water couldn't give birth to a Feline like her. Where were her real parents?
Tangtang couldn't make sense of it. She spent days comparing herself to everyone in the Stockade. Some were too sturdy, others too short. Not a single one had ears or a tail as beautiful as hers.
This dilemma weighed on Tangtang for quite some time, until Ruan Lin called her over for ironpot stewed fin. Tangtang glanced at Ruan Yi's bowl, then at her own. The head, eyes, and tender belly of the fin were all in hers. As she picked out the fin belly and stuffed it into Ruan Lin's mouth, she thought to herself: "Why should I care about what the Stockaders yammer about 'mommy's touch'? Dad's cooking is delish and that's enough for me!"

After extensive investigation and verification, the HR Division confirmed that Tangtang was still an unweaned babe when she was found. Given the physiologies of a newborn, it would have been impossible for her to drift far along the river. Therefore, it is preliminarily inferred that she was abandoned somewhere close to Qingbo Stockade.
After conducting detailed examinations and evaluations of her eye, Medical Division personnel suspect that the pattern within it is closely linked to her Originium Arts. Given the pattern's high degree of regularity, it can be ruled out as a random symptom arising from Oripathy infection. Instead, it is more likely related to her familial medical history. However, after reviewing all preserved personnel records of Qingbo Stockade, no individuals with similar conditions to hers were found.
To quote her own account: "I just practiced and practiced by the water, and this pattern appeared by itself."
This is absolutely impossible. We sought assistance from HAS, and after reviewing resident archives, they were likewise unable to identify Tangtang's relatives. However, a Tianshi specializing in Yan history made a breakthrough: within the Yan documents passed down from Terra, she discovered records highly relevant to the pattern in Tangtang's eye. According to legendary accounts in the literature, this pattern symbolizes the evolution of heaven and earth, containing ancient knowledge inheritance. Yet Tangtang clearly lacks access to such learning. The Tianshi of Wuling were equally astonished by this discovery. They had never imagined that such a unique user of Originium Arts existed right within their reach.
In conclusion, the specific reasons behind Tangtang's abandonment in Qingbo Stockade ... may be more complex than we initially assumed.
...
After we shared the investigation findings with Tangtang, she simply scratched her head and said her origins weren't all that important. After all, she had family and friends now, living a good life. Though she did wonder, just a little, if she still has blood relatives, and how they might be faring ... She emphasized it was just a little, about the size of a small shellbeast's claw.
Tangtang still keeps the small swaddling cloth she was wrapped in back then. When handing the fabric over to us, she noticeably hesitated for a moment before returning to her usual carefree demeanor: "And remember to give it back once you're done checking!"

In the beginning, children at the Den of the Brave always poked fun at Adelheid. No one really knew the girl who lived so far away. She was shy, introverted, dressed in boring clothing, slow to react, and never caught the ball during conversations. "Biggie" Tom started by badmouthing her at every turn. He wanted her out of the children's secret base. But Tom eventually relented because of two reasons: The grown-ups respected the Caprinae couple who adopted Adelheid, and even though she was teary eyed and sniveling, she never forgot about stuffing herself with apple peelings and turnip leaves. 

Everything changed in that atrocious summer. The rains poured in June, the entire place was flooded, and the bandits were finally evicted after a grueling battle. The ordeal left scars upon five families who lost their loved ones. The unsuspecting children followed the procession to the suburbs, and they saw her atop the hills. Adelheid, except it was not the little crybaby they knew. They saw the girl and her family cleaning out the resting places, cleaning the headstones, and offering elegies to the deceased. It was not until the coffin was laid to rest when the children finally realized that Tom would no longer return to Den of the Brave. 
Instead of fear, it was panic and denial that spread. The children could not accept the machinations of fate, and failed to figure out a way to make up for the missing position. It was then when Adelheid placed a simple wooden statuette before Tom's grave. It was very roughly carved, crooked, imbalanced, and unpolished. 
"He always wanted a figurine of a Competition Knight," the girl said. "That would be Tom's final wish." 
The grown-ups fail to control their tears again. They lamented the death of a life so innocent and young. 
But the children tried not to laugh as the statuette looked nothing like a Competition Knight. 
In the end, they bore it no longer and burst out laughing. 
They took out their Knight Cards and discussed how to make the statuette more knight-like. Although Adelheid failed to follow their conversation and the task of carving the figurine fell to a more dexterous companion, the children would always hand the new and much improved statuette into Adelheid's hands, for she was tasked with leading their own procession into the cemetery and perform the annual ceremony. 
"Tom is right here," the girl promised every year. 
No one knew how Adelheid was so certain about this, or how she learned of Tom's wishes. Nobody seemed to care about how she performed her work. 

In the end, Adelheid did not break her shell. She remained rather inept at expressing herself. Every time her tummy rumbled, she became so embarrassed she would start inching to a nearby dustbin. But whenever new kids arrive in town and start talking about the strange girl humming songs in the bushes, someone would tap them on the shoulder and give them a quite a story.

What sets her apart isn't just her expertise, but her perseverance, fearless spirit, and above all, her genuine love for science and unquenchable curiosity. Without dedicated researchers like her, we might never truly understand the world we live in. 
You'll often find her venturing out alone — collecting samples, studying geological structures, and transforming observations into theories. Thanks to her efforts, Endfield has gained a much deeper understanding of Talos-II's geology and the threats posed by the Blight. Her research has laid the groundwork for emergency plans in case of Blight outbreaks. I have great respect for Ardelia — for her humility, grace, and unwavering sense of purpose. It's as if she carries an endless well of strength, always certain of the path she must follow.

Ever since Tianshi Zhuang came aboard the Dijiang, there's been one more workaholic buried in the labs. 
The Tianshi approaches her work with great enthusiasm. Every day, she packs her schedule herself, ticking off each task without wasting a second. Her home back in Wuling City stays spotless — so clean it feels as though no one has ever lived there. In contrast, her lab is cluttered with personal items, as if that's where life actually happens. 
If not for HAS stepping in and ordering a mandatory break, Tianshi Zhuang would never have put down her work. Some feared that the sheer amount of work would soon leave Tianshi Zhuang collapsed at the lab bench. What they failed to realize was that she actually found the lack of work to be more unbearable. 
On the first day of her forced vacation, she gave an illusion of rest. But soon, restlessness crept into her expression, and stillness gave way to anxiety. She started pacing up and down the beach, worrying about everything back in the lab. 
With each passing day of the break, her mood grew heavier. By the end, Tianshi Zhuang who could barely get out of bed kept murmuring these words: "The lab ... I need to get back to the lab. The results could come in any moment. I cannot waste any more time." 
After the break was finally over, she returned to the lab with a smile so radiant that people thought she had a really beautiful vacation. In truth, she was only glad that the ordeal by vacation was over. Even Perlica, another widely recognized workaholic, was astonished by Tianshi Zhuang's professional commitment. 
There is a reason she works the way she does. She isn't the only one waiting for the results. The entire HAS, and Talos-II itself, are watching her progress closely. 
As rift disasters grow ever more frequent and devastating, every moment Tianshi Zhuang spends at work carries the possibility of a new solution. Her time is no longer hers alone, but generously sacrificed for those who have lost homes and lives to the rifts. She dare not, and she cannot allow even a second to go to waste.

"How long are you gonna stay this time? You coming home?" 
"...A day. And nah." 
"Just a day? Then never mind ... sigh. Well, a couple of days ago, Rossi was whining again, saying she thinks you'll pull the same stunt this year — you know, 'the gift arrives, but the brother doesn't.' Come on, even if you're not planning to come home, you could at least find time to see her once in a while." 
"It's already been what, over half a year? Since you two last met up at Tommaso's place." 
"I still need to take care of a few things. Once it's done..." 
"Stop right there! That's what you said last time! Then you ran off to the frontier, saying you had to clean up someone's mess..." 
"Gosh, I don't get you young folks. How do you always have so much to do?" 
"Hey, if I were you, no matter how swamped I was, I'd still swing by more to check in on my little sis. She's a kid! Every other kid her age in the clan's doted on by their families all day every day..." 
"You're her family too." 
"Well, yeah — Wait! No, don't try to spin this on me... I get you've got your own things going on. But listen, as someone who's been there — whenever I see little Rossi, I can't help but think of my own little girl... Biggest regret of my life? Not being there for her when I still had the chance." 
"Just hear me out, Catello... Life's short, don't do things you'll end up regretting." 
"I hear you. Uncle Rust."  
"Rossi knows I'm back today." 
"WHAT? No way!" 
"Then why would she run off to the hunting grounds first thing in the morning with the Louis twins? Unless..." 
"Uh-huh. Exactly." 
"Argh... You two really are true Lupus. So stubborn and so damn alike ... it's scary." 
"Alright, alright. Do whatever you like! But if you're always absent, aren't you worried something might go wrong?" 
"I was gonna keep it from you for Rossi's sake ... but looks like you need to hear it. Six months ago, she got herself into serious trouble — stuck her neck out for Old Bart and his men, and ended up on the Shadowskull's hit list. I remember it clear as day. Fourteen of them showed up, each nastier than the last. If Tommaso hadn't pulled some strings and brought in Capone's Fangs, we probably wouldn't have even made it out of the black market alive..." 
"..." 
"Worried now, huh?" 
"Nope. I was just wondering how Rossi found out I was heading north. It was you, wasn't it?" 
"Oh! Um, heh ... well ... yeah, I might've let that slip ... wasn't on purpose though..." 
"Ahem, anyway! I checked your guns! They're as good as new! Just ease up on those custom rounds of yours. No barrel's gonna last with the way you burn through them..." 
"Got it." 
"And ... there were actually fifteen of them." 
"Huh?" 
"Alright, see you around." 
— Audio log from Howlfire Gunsmiths

DOCUMENT: A medical record often reviewed by Akekuri 
BASIC INFO 
PATIENT NAME: Estella Kerr 
POSITION: Member of Operations Team Z7; full-time operator, Endfield Industries. 
OPERATIONAL CODENAME: Estella 
ROUTE OF ADMISSION: Combat UAV ambulance 
ADMISSION TIME: 2307 
ADMISSION LOCATION: Endfield wildlands medical station, Valley III 

CHIEF COMPLAINT 
Hit by an explosion. Multiple open and bleeding wounds. Shock after 45 minutes of intense pain. 

PRESENT ILLNESS 
Patient was conducting recon operations 5 klicks away from the site of the explosion but exercised personal initiative in changing the operational plan 45 minutes ago. Patient charged into a cross-firing zone to cover the retreat of trapped teammates but was exposed to enemy's suppressive fire. Patient described that she has been knocked off her feet by a blast and temporarily lost consciousness. She then crawled for about 20 meters before other teammates of Op Z7 discovered her and quickly sent her on medevac. 

MEDICAL HISTORY 
Healthy. Denies chronic illnesses, past surgeries, and past blood transfusions. Oripathy negative. 

PHYSIOLOGICAL EXAMINATION (AT ADMISSION) 
Clouded consciousness, pallor, grimacing in pain 
VITAL SIGNS: Normal temperature. Weak pulse. Blood pressure slightly below average. Weak breathing. 
HEAD: Open laceration (4 cm) at left temporal fossa. Cortical bone intact. No fractures. 
NECK: No tracheal deviations. Observable collapse of jugular vein when supine. 
CHEST: Penetrating wound of right rib cage, diameter about 1.2 cm. Percussion reveals tympany. Diminished breath sounds. Muffled heart sounds, no arrhythmia. 
ABDOMEN: Distension and tenderness of lower right abdomen. 
LIMBS: Open mid-shaft fracture of left femur, open wound measuring 6 cm long, end of bone visible; Penetrating wound of posterolateral aspect of right calf, pressure dressing already applied to site of bleeding; Weakened arterial pulse in lower extremities 
SKIN & MUCOSA: Multiple abrasions and contusions 

PRELIMINARY DIAGNOSIS 
RIGHT SIDE: Open pneumothorax 
Hemorrhagic shock (Lv.Ⅲ) 
Open fracture (type Ⅲ) of left femur 
Multiple penetrating wounds of soft tissue 
Light blunt trauma of cranium 

LIST OF EMERGENCY RESPONSES 
Open pneumothorax treatment 
Blood volume resuscitation 
Anti-shock treatment 
Pain management treatment 
Anti-Oripathy measures 
Dressing of wounds on left thigh and right calf 
Tetanus vaccination 

PROGNOSTIC ASSESSMENT 
Patient has been transferred to the Endfield Medical Division after emergency treatment 
According to combat trauma assessments, patient has 85% survival rate for the next 24 hours 
If hemodynamics remain stable and no subsequent infections occur, physical training and rehab can proceed after 6-8 weeks 

VISITATION RECORDS

"Mr. Catcher! You're finally here! Your name is in the recipient's section, but we all believe that you should come by and verify the package in person... It's now in the unloading area. Yes, the biggest package there! Right next to the facility scale model that Mr. Andre purchased."

"Sure. No problem. Let me take a look... Address is somewhere in Seš'qa and the sender is ... Cassandra? Sounds really familiar to me..." 
"...Got it. The package is mine." 
"Are ... are you really sure? Routine inspections found that someone has specifically cast anti-tracking Originium Arts upon this thing." 
"Don't worry. The package is really meant for me... My older sister sent it to me. She has a habit of applying protective measures given the nature of her work." 
"Your sister? Wait! I remember... Is she that Cassandra? Cassandra of the Mist? That famous bodyguard who made her name while working for Seš'qa merchants?!" 
"Yeah." 
"Fine... I think I know where she's coming from. The 'protective measures' might be necessary, then." 
............ 
"Phewie. Processing is complete. Mr. Catcher, you're free to take this parcel." 
"Can I open it here?" 
"Of course you can! In fact, we can also give you delivery support if you need help carrying it." 
............ 
"Wha — What the hell is this?! Is this some type of ... exoskeletal frame?!" 
"...Stop, Mr. Catcher! What's that thing you're holding in your hand? Maybe you should only press the button at a more spacious—" 
(Recorded audio file starts to play) 
"Ruy, baby, got the prez?" 
"Sorry. Too much work is catching up to your sis. I'm afraid I can't celebrate your birthday at your place." 
"Ay, caramba. When I heard our broder said he got an urgent order to head north, I planned to take a few days off but the boss suddenly got us a major order that cuts through the middle of nowhere. I had to do this myself..." 
"So I got you the latest civilian-grade U-47 Heavy Exoskeleton for your birthday this year. Hurhur. It's far cooler than the DIY alloy greatsword that broder gave you last time, right?" 
"Anyway, people say you got plenty of field missions, so I applied for a 5-year warranty. Wear it when you head out. It'll make Papa and Mama feel safer..." 
"You know. Papa and Mama never feared anything except you getting hurt by accident and ending up like last time..." 
"So please pay close attention to your health. Don't forget the promise you made to me and our broder. And don't forget what Papa and Mama told you, k?" 
"Finally, happy birthday, Ruy. You're the baby broder I am always worried about." 
"Your sister will always keep you in my heart." 
(End of recorded audio file)

DOCUMENT: Two Photographs
An old photograph with yellowing edges, featuring Pogranichnik standing amongst a diverse crew of various races. The group stood before a fortified defense works forged of steel and covered by snow. Two Oathkeeper scouts stood atop the defenses, gazing into the far distance with binoculars. BACKGROUND: Contours of a fort could be seen in the slightly blurred horizon, along with large caliber cannons pointing at the skies. CHARACTERS OF NOTE: A particular crew mate standing next to Pogranichnik wore an expression of pride that stood out from the others. The man pointed at the skies where a giant vessel floated above everything. This photograph does not show the entirety of the said vessel. 

A photograph of a great hall within a fort, taken from above. Soldiers of the Order of Steel Oath who stood in the middle of the hall raised their cups into the air at Pogranichnik who stood on the stage. UPPER LEFT: Progranichnik placing a fist on the massive map behind him. UPPER RIGHT: A long dining table. A silvery haired old man with a chiseled face, though the features were obscured as he faced the other way. All those seated at the table wore badges and sashes of banner commanders, and like the soldiers, they also raised their glasses. LOWER LEFT: Young recruits rubbing shoulders with each other. One of them played an accordion and those nearby seemed to be singing and cheering loudly with their mouths open. NOTE: The hall is filled with plenty of individuals in festive spirits, but Pogranichnik never showed the picture to anyone, and neither did he frame it. 

DOCUMENT: Three Recipes
Entrée Recipe C5: Primal Cut Burdenbeast Steak Set. Courtesy of UWST. A primal cut of burdenbeast shank, nutrient-fortified, smoked. Standard UWST Guards military fare. Winner of the United Workers' Syndicates of Talos II Central Production Planning Committee Awards for 20 consecutive years. 
"The Shieldguards are still getting used to the unique taste of the fortifying agents. Besides that, this is most impeccable as field rations. It offers sufficient calories, nutrition, and the fillet has been prepared to provide an excellent texture — I remember tasting something similar before, something from Ursus." 

Entrée Recipe C8: Metal Crab Doria Set. Courtesy of TGCC. La Fantoma metal crabs and Kjersch cheese come together in this preparation by master chefs of Neo Tsukushi. This is designed to create explosions of freshness that blend the Talosian hills and oceans. A gastronomic experience fitting for the indomitable Oathkeepers. 
"A culinary wonder rarely seen in self-cooking rations. They are quite effective in maintaining the morale of the fighting banners. However, caloric content of this particular item is currently incapable of meeting the Shieldguards' requirements. Please improve upon it." 

Entrée Recipe C12: Instant Shangshu Hot Pot. Courtesy of HAS. These words were messily scribbled on the back of the rations crate: "Khorsyn, your soldiers are battle-hardened veterans. And what do you feed them with? Trough slop so stale that they're crying FOWL! Since you've been most respectful to this tianshi, this entire crate is on me. Guranteed to dispel the cold and put heat in your guts. Don't forget to warm the burdo-tallow for the grease dip." 
"This entrée has utterly decimated my warriors. Half of the Shieldguards in the entire banner cried out for painkillers. A number of them managed to find strength to crawl on the ground and stuff handfuls of snow in their mouths. However, no one in the banner complained about the cold in the 30-klick foot march." 

DOCUMENT: A Map 
A massive map illustrated on massive piece of tanned cystybeast hide. It was made just in case all instruments and machinery running on Originium technology fail. 
The map is densely marked with Order of Steel Oath defense zones, supply routes, and key strong points. Arsenals of Fort Forgefane have been included as well. 
The southern area of the map shows dozens of roads meandering along the contours that connect the various Order forts. A few of these routes pass through Myrkwood — lifelines that connect the Civilization Band to the Order of Steel Oath and the very edge of the Northern Corridor. The northern area of the map shows a jagged battle line that stretches across the land like a scar. It stretches from the main defense zones of the Order and ends only at the fringe of the Aurora. 
In the memo section furnished next to the map display rack, Pogranichnik, the author of this map, left this handwritten message: 
1,237 names. That's the worth of this.

No Op Z7 teammates, except for Estella, have positive memories regarding the anniversary for the Founding of Operations Team Z7. However, everyone agrees that it was an unforgettable occasion. 
At first, Akekuri found that the team had no field assignments on the day of the anniversary and suggested celebrating the occasion. Everyone responded positively and a discussion on the means of celebration began. However, since the team was encamped in the wildlands far from the Civilization Band, every suggestion involved some form of outdoor activity. Estella, unwilling to engage in any physical exertion, naturally voted against every single proposal. In the end, "riverside picnic" was the only option that received a unanimous vote. It was not the favorite option for everyone, but at least nobody voted against it. 
On the day of the anniversary, everyone was eagerly gathering herbs and hunting game. Estella, however, returned with an armful of colorful mushrooms. Her teammates firmly rejected her suggestion to toss those wild fungi into the cooking pot. In the end, the team conceded. Under Captain Akekuri's watchful eyes, several unassuming mushrooms were allowed to be part of the stew. 
As the sun set, the team built a campfire by the river to enjoy what they had gathered throughout the day. Fortunately, the "unassuming" mushrooms turned out to be only mildly toxic. Unfortunately, they were incredibly spicy. The team emptied their water canteens to douse the heat but to no avail. Desperate, they rushed to the riverbank to wash the spicy taste away with river water. That's when they heard a low rumble coming from upstream — the dam had begun a reservoir drawdown! 
"Curses! I forgot about the UWST reservoir drawdown notice! That's why there's no field operations today!" 
No one remembered exactly how they ended up swept away by the floodwaters. When they finally came to, they found Estella skillfully surfing the rushing water on the team's cooking pot. The sun had already set when the four Op Z7 teammates pulled each other to shore. They had no choice but head downstream to look for Estella. Finally, the team found Estella sound asleep at a nomad campfire in wee hours of the morning. The nomads treated Akekuri and her team to a proper wildlands feast. 
The nomads were extremely accommodating and the team decided to rest there for the night. Just as Akekuri was about to fall asleep beneath the starry ceiling, she suddenly remembered a Z7 field assignment in a few hours' time. Estella could not be awakened, so the four Z7 teammates took turns carrying her. They successfully reached the Endfield camp at daybreak. 
According to Estella's memories, she was completely unconscious as she probably ate the other fungi she picked. She treated the flood waters as a packed and riotous moshpit, and fantasized herself as a rockstar performing a stage dive and surfing the crowd while she growled and screamed her songs. Nobody knew what Estella sang. Akekuri only remembered how she carried Estella and trudged back to camp. The young girl on her back did mumble a few things while she slept — things about home.

DOCUMENT: A prayer slip, kept within a book 
O merciful Lord, I praise thee. 
Grant language onto me, but lead me not into voicing it with vulgar words. 
Grant intellect onto me, but lead me not into employing it for blasphemy. 
Grant benevolence onto me, but lead me not into abusing it with arrogance. 
Grant vision onto me, but lead me not into corrupting it with base and common images. 
Grant friendship onto me, but lead me not into terminating it with violence. 
Grant eternal curiosity onto me, but lead me not into wasting it with ignorance. 
(NOTE: After verification, prayers of every Cabalist are based on their most truthful desires. The Cabal of Tranquility encourages their members to compose their own prayers. The followers of the Lord have their own belief and will about the Lord. And that is how they define their faith.) 

DOCUMENT: Excerpt from a diary 
Four years have passed since I boarded this vessel. The task of repair is progressing slowly, but with efficacy. Although the undertaking has become relatively uneventful, I have gradually found my way to return to my inner calm. This is the place where I can work in a dark and cold cabin. The rhythms of machines offer me incredible comfort. This is where I need not worry whether my actions would bring trouble to the others. Of course, this is also where I can share fragmented conversations with data residues of the Originium Network. In the Network, I experienced never-seen-before ruins of splendorous majesty that Sankta share their empathy. I heard the lamentations from myriad souls of the Sarkaz erased from existence. I witnessed the incessant bleeding of rebellion and subservience. And every time I wanted to take another step, these experiences would suddenly cease. The silence is frightening. I continued my calculations and repairs, hoping I can hear it speak once more. 
............ 
Something I feared even more has happened. I realized that the Originium has been polluted, damaged, and obliterated. It seems intertwined with what I perused in the various tomes of the Cabal. But why is this the case? What does Originium mean with regards to the codes of civilization that we are deciphering? And what is the entity capable of polluting, damaging, and even obliterating the Originium? 
Perhaps this is why Abbess Mumu sent me here. 
............ 
That was the day when I noticed a strange glow on Supervisor Perlica's visage. But this glow was quickly extinguished by her constant pondering. They are whispering. Something big is about to happen. Will it be relevant to the answers I seek? 
............ 
Black hair, black mask, and black shadow. Operator Chen Qianyu introduced the Endministrator to me. The one who had been hibernating in the medical bay. 
And for an instant, I seemed to achieve a form of empathy. A cacophony and impulse for joy, laughter, and tears exploded within me. I could not restrain the shaking of my material form. This entity is the answer, but I have not prepared my questions.

Grandma: 
I have received the package from you. The new Arts Unit is just what I need to support my modified orbiter. I have distributed the other local specialties that came attached with the package. There is no need for you to send these things to me. I have a fixed salary good enough that I have some leftover after purchasing parts for engineering mods every month. 
I know you've sent plushes of movie characters, outfits of classic movie stars, and other limited edition movie posters so that I can use these to befriend other individuals. You have been doing this since I was attending the academy — However, those classmates of mine simply stashed the collectibles they received inside their closets and never showed them again. Your following letter told me not to be sad. I really wasn't, grandmother. It is just like what I've told you. Their reactions and responses will not influence my attitude towards them. 
My colleagues at Endfield are not like the classmates I have in the academy. The Endfielders never turned me down nor rejected my ideas. Life is here is good, and I enjoy more liberties. There is something else that I intend to tell you. My communication skills have vastly improved thanks to the instructions provided by my Z7 teammates and constant side-by-side training offered by the Endministrator. 
You once worried that my personality might start to conflict with my superior, but my current situation proves your worries are unnecessary. Our meetings have been enjoyable and the Endmin happily accepts everything I share. This also explains why I have been writing less to you. You no longer need to be concerned about my lack of friends. It is not about taking and giving, but mutual sincerity to explore and discuss everything about each other... I believe I have completely understood the true meaning of "friendship". 
Also, your request for passing on a message to the Endministrator has been carried out by me. The Endmin is enthusiastic and even said that the meeting with you should have taken place much earlier. 

Antal

Mr. Dolly's Game II 
The geology of Talos-II... unlike the volcanoes she knew, brimming with the vitality of expansion, eruption, and flow. Under erosion, it showed more of corrosion, withering, and consumption. The rock layers lost their logic, the earth as if diseased. Its skin peeled away, veins twisted, some areas warped by aberration. 
Ardelia came to study the Blight, to keep pace with its unpredictable spread. She often ventured into high-risk zones alone, turning her life into lists of tasks. 
She started to speak less, no longer weaving her thoughts into poetry. Her voice grew quieter, meals were often forgotten, and at night her fists clenched unconsciously in her sleep. The things she had fought so hard to protect — her eyes, her ears, the rhythm of her pulse, now filled her with a quiet unease. The health she had regained was slowly being eroded by an unseen dread. 
"How much time do I have left?" she wondered. It wasn't death she feared, it was a desperate race against the crumbling of this strange new land. 
Until that day Mr. Dolly leapt out from a shallow pit. 
He knocked over her rock hammer and snatched the instrument case. Ardelia followed, shouting in vain. They ran farther and farther — off-route, off-plan. She was supposed to be surveying a newly-formed Blight rift, but instead, she found herself in a quiet valley, sheltered by cliffs. 
A vast outcrop of columnar igneous rock stretched before her. Hexagonal pillars rose from the ground like piano keys. Beneath her feet lay ancient volcanic ruins, so well-preserved it was as if time had paused. 
That familiar spark kindled in her heart once more. Ardelia knelt down, pulled out her notebook, and began to sketch — not for a mission, nor for data, but simply because it was beautiful and captivating. 
That evening, Ardelia and Mr. Dolly made camp nearby. A cool breeze whispered through the air as stars rose between the jagged rock spires. Mr. Dolly, curled at her feet, let out a sneeze, sending her pen cap tumbling into the grass. 
"You led me here on purpose, didn't you?" 
Mr. Dolly didn't answer. It rolled over and tapped her boot with its leg. 
"You think I've stopped being myself... that all I do now is worry, racing against the Blight." 
"But I'm scared, too. Scared that if I slow down, even for a moment ... it'll be too late." 
She ran her fingers along Mr. Dolly's back and closed her eyes. The warmth of its fur against her palm was so comforting that for the first time, she slept soundly and sweetly under the open sky. 
The next morning, she logged in her journal: 
"Ancient volcanic ruins discovered in the northeast. Columnar joints well preserved." 
"Led here by Mr. Dolly. Reconnected with my love for geology. Mood: content." 
"Note to self: Slow down. Stay healthy."

"Why?"
The legendary senior business consultant of Seš'qa, one of the lead brand managers of the Witching Hour, the downtrodden Sarkaz merchant, "Bridge Builder" Fleming, was taken aback by this simple question. Though it came right out of the blue, Fleming quickly regained his cool, tidied his tie, and started counting the stars as he readied himself for the banter. 
The Feline who stood before him always made him tingle with a strange nervousness, ever since that snowy night. 
"Ahem. First thing first... We genuinely appreciate Endfield's acceptance of Adelheid. Seš'qa hereby extends its most sincere gratitude." 
"Good. That means you'll pay extra for her additional catering fees. Right?" 
"Trust me. Sending her to Endfield is considered a loss for our business." 
"Oh. You have a slogan for Last Rite ... the Princess of the War Court? Very loud and attention grabbing. Must have made you a fortune." 
Fleming laughed. He usually laughs as a means of dealing with his opponent on the negotiating table. But at this moment, he was laughing to give himself a chance to breathe. 
M3 paid no attention to Fleming's peculiarities. Her gaze was reserved for Adelheid, seated uncomfortably outside the office — Last Rite herself. Fleming sensed M3's curiosity. He cannot afford to miss the opportunity to regain his initiative. 
"What do you think of Miss Last Rite?" 
"I think she's hungry," M3 said without averting her gaze from the girl in question. Fleming tried to remember things. Rumors speak of the Feline's ties with the origins of Kazdel, and she hardly paid this much attention to other talents he recommended. "How could you let such a lovely girl starve?" 
"I swear..." 
"I think you need to pay an additional catering fee to Endfield Industries. Maybe we should set this sum to..." 
"I *SWEAR* this is for the best!" 
Fleming immediately realized that he had slipped. His opponent was simply trying to muddy the waters... No. She was just having a friendly banter. Why did he suddenly break his composure? 
"And why is that?" 
"Ugh... You know, a Nachzehrer in a cemetery with an extreme 'shame of consuming'... She has consistently refused to touch the deaths of others. Her constant hunger is only a natural consequence." 
"No, no, no... You got it all wrong..." 
M3 maintained her coy, relaxed tone. But that was not the worst for Fleming. What stressed him out more was the fact that she had not smiled ever since he stepped aboard Dijiang. 
"You know the Sarkaz. No amount of roasted steak fillets could fill an empty soul." 
"Soul? You believe in souls?" 
"Ahem... Every Sarkaz who benefited from the protection of the myriad souls believes in them." 
"I'm sure the myriad souls will be happy to know that," M3 finally moved her gaze away from the girl. She hesitated, a rare opportunity. But Fleming did not treat this as a good sign, "But the time does not match." 
"I understand... It took place over a century ago. Nevertheless, Adelheid is definitely a young girl of only seventeen or eighteen years." 
"Right. So, why?" 
Fleming kept his bitter smile inside. Nevertheless, he decided to confront this question directly. 
"I don't know. But like you said ... she remains very hungry." 
"Even with 'that thing' following her around? That's practically unheard of." 
That genuinely surprised Fleming, if only a little. "Find it rather astonishing that there are things you have not heard about." 
Fleming immediately regretted it when those words blurted out of his mouth. Thankfully, M3 was not in the leisurely mood to interpret his verbal mishap as a taunt. 
"A vast land has perished in her shadow. Millennia-worth of winters heed her beck and call. Yet she remains hungry." 
"It's the blood. We found other Nachzehrers. So many deaths are birthed upon this planet everyday. We have no desire to see another War Court appear without warning. But ... this child is obviously an exception. She has not been 'fed' because she respects every crew mate, messenger, and soldier who died in the frontiers. She could not bring herself to do it. In fact, she refuses to do it." 
"Then how did her power..." 
"'Though she did not consume the dead to strengthen herself, Death remains willing to assist her.' That wendigo friend of yours gave this assessment." 
"...Nezzsalem would be extremely moved if he were here." 
"But that also means the child is destined to take on burdens that shouldn't be hers." 
"I suppose this is the actual reason you recommended her to Endfield." 
"If Adelheid hopes to take upon a path of her choice, I believe Endfield Industries will be her best instructor." 
M3 was obviously taken aback. Fleming himself was also stunned by her reaction. He knew that M3 never expected him to give such a ... soft and compassionate answer. However, he also did not expect M3 to had judged him so poorly. It was a depressing realization for the merchant and consultant. 
"Well, Fleming ... perhaps you are kinder than I thought." 
Those words allowed Fleming's confidence to return. 
"And that is also your kindest evaluation of my character for all these years we've known each other, Miss M3." 
M3 sighed. It would seem she finally allowed herself to relax. "Now, how would you like Endfield to treat her?" 
"The usual," Fleming smiled from the bottom of his heart for the first time in this dialog. "Let her do what she wants, like a normal child. Let her live, get into trouble, grow up, and earn her keep. It would be wonderful if she gets to make a few friends and discover what she wants out of life..." 
"Treating her as your own?" 
"Hah. Me? My blood's too poor for her," Fleming also shifted his gaze to the window. Adelheid was already getting overwhelmed by other Endfield operators trying to start a conversation with her. 
"But before Talos-II forces humanity to the brink of extinction, before Death completely fashions her bloodied throne, and before the next Sovereign of the Nachzehrers is forced to manifest upon this planet ... she simply remains as a shy little Sarkaz girl."

DOCUMENT: Alesh's Daily Routine 
06:00: Wakes up. Prepares angling gear and bait. Sharpens the hooks while mumbling to himself: "Gotta really hook these fins today." 
06:30: Sets off. Throws some fin bones to the cloudbeast strays in the streets. 
06:45-09:15: Morning angling time. Finds a place where water flow is slower. Waits patiently for the fins. 
09:15-10:00: Wraps up the angling gear. Checks his catch. Inspects the conditions of the caught fins. "Special" catches are set aside for other uses. 
10:00-12:00: Fin stall morning shift. Fins are arranged neatly in a specific number of rows and directions. These details matter a lot. 
12:00-13:00: Lunch time. Roasted fin over fire. Eats while glancing at his handyterm. 
13:00-15:00: Takes a nap or walk. Sometimes goes off to the wharf to review his angling skills, or sits on the bench to talk to strangers on proper angling spots. Jabbers on and on while making the fins restless in the water. 
15:00-17:30: Fin stall afternoon shift. Continues selling fins while observing the passers by for any "familiar faces" that shouldn't be showing up. 
17:45-19:45: Night angling at deeper waters. Final push during sunset. Specifically targets "great fins" that tend to be cautious and alert. These specimens are most active during sunset. This is also the time when enemies are most likely to make their mistakes. 
20:00-21:00: Dinner time. Organizes his catch for the day. Records the angling results and daily "fintel" he gathered from all that talking. 
21:00-22:00: Rest time. Relaxes on the balcony and gazes at the stars with his only eye. Occasionally gets reminded of those eventful nights... The turf wars are distant memories, yet they also felt like undercurrents that could suddenly snag him while he angles. 
22:00: Prepares the bait. Checks his angling gear. "Who'll be the fin for tomorrow?" 

Anecdotes about Alesh
The new liaison arrived at the secret locale at the corner of the wharf for the first time. The owner of the fin stall laid motionless on a bench with a book on his face. 
The fins being sold had been laid out in a specific arrangement — grayfins faced north; red cupras were paired, and tucked away at the corner was a strangely patterned whitefin. The liaison blinked as he worked his mind to recall the fincode he memorized. Struggle as he could, he failed to read the intel. Just as he was about to call the headquarters, the stall owner tossed him a fin with bits of crushed ice. 
"No great fins today," he said, "Settle your nutritional needs with this one." 
The liaison was stunned for two seconds before he accepted the fin and nodded in gratitude. He walked for around thirty yards before turning around and looked at the stall again — The owner laid on his bench as though the transaction had never taken place. 
Report of the day: Situation normal. Intel is accurate and ... pretty reliable.

DOCUMENT: A private letter 
Eyrwin: 
Maybe I should call you Snowshine now. In any case, please forgive me for not saying goodbye when I left the team... That was never my intention. But my captain and my attending surgeon, Margarit, told me to leave the north immediately. They said it would prevent my hallucinations from getting worse. 
Kjersch is a beautiful city. We don't see any auroras here but there are equally majestic mountains in snow. The ridges are untouched by the Blight or the Aggeloi, and are linked by criss-crossing cable tramways that the city is so famous for — I took quite a few rides in them, and the experience of gazing into the vast snowfields without worry is unforgettable... 
You must have been surprised by my decision. Someone who had sworn to stay in the north and the SAR team for eternity ... was suddenly beaten by a most mundane and ordinary blizzard. What I want to say is that sometimes people are not as strong as they like to think. Perhaps I'm actually more fragile than I think I was. 
I never feared blizzards, the Blight, or any other disasters that could suddenly swoop in and take our lives. But when I saw Nelson lose a leg after getting sucked into the Blight while trying to save that unlucky prospector ... and after learning that Lisa lost her sight from overexerting her Originium Arts to give everyone an early warning... I started doubting myself. I began to think if I had fallen short ... and my suspicions soon spread to other members of the team... 
I have the captain to thank. I was about to use the Arts Unit when he stopped me and ordered Medical Officer Margarit to give Ryder the timely treatment he needed... He saved me from doing something I would've regretted for the rest of my life. Eyrwin, of all the young people on the team, I have the highest expectations for you. In fact, I believe you are the perfect candidate to succeed as deputy captain. You value friendship and care for others deeply, often to the point of neglecting your own safety. So take this as advice from someone who's been through it: never forget to look after yourself, especially when you're out there saving others. 
You are important and irreplaceable to the SAR team and everyone who cares for you. 
I look forward to your reply. Feel free to let me play the host in your visit to Kjersch. And try to bring the captain along. I'll take you all to the best fondue in town. It tastes exactly like what you described to me. 

Madeleine Crick 

DOCUMENT: A private letter 
Madeleine: 
Thank you for writing to me! 
Even now, I still remember your patience when you first taught me how to build an igloo shelter in the snowfields; your stern expression when you reminded me that every SAR teammate must maintain constant vigilance; and your tenderness when you helped me fix my drone at 4 AM, telling me to be more careful next time. These are precious memories I'll carry with me for the rest of my life... 
So, I have never doubted your passion for SAR operations. Even though you have left the north, I believe you're still helping everyone at your new place in your own special ways. 
Ryder and the captain refused to tell me what exactly happened on the mountain, but I could sort of guess from the operational logs... I don't think they, or anyone for that matter, would blame you for this. So I hope you can focus on getting better, and don't forget to explore the place when have time. Once I swing by Kjersch (captain seems pretty busy and I couldn't get hold of him) I'll definitely pay you a visit. And is that fondue place really as good as you say? I really wanna try it out! 
P.S. The pack that came with this letter is your favorite sundried berries. Eat them before they expire! 

Eyrwin
