[Clinical Diagnosis Report]
Imaging scans indicate blurred organ contours with observable abnormal shadows within the operator's body. Detection of Originium particles within the circulatory system shows anomalies, presenting signs of Oripathy. At this stage, the operator can be confirmed as an Oripathy-positive.

Attending Physician's Note: According to Tangtang's own account, she contracted Oripathy during a conflict between Qingbo Stockade and the Tianshi of Wuling City a decade ago. Tangtang stated she received no specialized treatment over these ten years, only various folk remedies provided sporadically by the stockade residents. However, examination results indicate that both her Cell-Originium Assimilation rate and Blood Originium-Crystal Density are remarkably well-controlled.
When questioned about this, Tangtang replied, "Everyone says I'm the River's Daughter. The water washes the sickness away."
Could natural bodies of water truly cure Oripathy? The answer is evident: it's impossible.

[Medication Application Form from a Tianshi]
Generic Medication Name: Oripathy Suppressant
Quantity Requested: Long-term supply
Infection Site of Patient: Ocular region
Reason for Application: Aiding Qingbo Stockade
Audio Log:
"Honestly, I'm a little hesitant about delivering the medication... The first time, he threw it right back at us, shouting, 'We won't take handouts from Wuling people!' and tried to charge at us with his head... Thankfully, the watchguards were there and helped us escape. I'm not afraid he'd kill me, it's just that we can't have another incident like that.
"The girl's Oripathy is on the verge of worsening. We're aware of it, and surely they are too. She contracted it because of us. We have an obligation to treat her.
"Back then ... it was sheer chaos. The sky was pitch black, low, and heavy with rain tearing through the curtain of clouds. We trudged through the howling wind as the stockade residents charged out from behind the hills, weapons in hand, their shadows in the night like malevolent spirits...
"People were terrified. No one noticed there was such a young child in the crowd...
"The rain washed away the blood... No, no, perhaps it never truly vanished. Whenever I close my eyes, I see that girl's wounded eye, and his ... the leader's eyes. The ones that said he just wanted to survive... I will never forget them for as long as I live.
"The second time, we left the syringes near the outskirts of Qingbo Stockade, where the residents were sure to pass by.
"This time, it wasn't charity from an enemy ... maybe it fell from the sky, grew from the earth, or was carried by a beast. Thinking of it that way might make it a little easier for them to accept.
"I waited two whole days ... and it was taken.
"I waited two more days and saw the girl playing by the water. She chased long-ears along the river for quite a distance. She seemed much better.
"I don't know what will happen from here on out ... and I don't think this counts as true atonement. But I had a full night's rest, at least for that day."

Senior Staff Officer Master Gruman, I, Intel Officer Roland Arlos, hereby report the relevant details of this battle pursuant to the orders of Castellan Zasso. 
The battle was a 7-day engagement. We committed the 4th and 6th Standards comprising 22 banners and 6,143 combatants. Over 42,000 Aggeloid entities and 32 Ankhors were eliminated. Multiple unregistered Aggeloid construct patterns were sighted in this conflict, with average combat capabilities approaching or exceeding the Homoiossaron. Most samples have been sent to the Grand Archives for categorization. (COMMENT: Samples received. Though I appreciate having more intact samples, I am also aware that my inputs would hardly affect what I actually get.) 
The following is a summary of the actual battle events — 
INTERCEPTION: 
2300 hours, February 10, Year 152: Sector West-2 of the Aurora Belt picked up Ankhor-level readings. The 4th Standard was assembled according to the Order Codex for emergency airlift. 
0005 hours, February 11: Interception operation initiated. 
0008 hours, February 11: Ankhorfall occurred ahead of schedule and entered a mobile orbit. The interception fleet missed the estimated interception point and failed to inflict sufficient damage to most of the Ankhors. 
(COMMENT: The biggest and most severe failure of this entire battle. Why was the early warning facility located so far outside? If the Ankhors were targeting somewhere further back, perhaps we had already missed our window of early interception. Have the monitoring stations been redeployed to better locations?) 
CONTACT: 
0500 hours, February 11: Forward elements have established a line of defense at the plateau of battle sector M-320a, and commenced Aggeloid host extermination according to scout intel. Said elements then proceed to push toward known Ankhor sites. 
1100 hours, February 11: A new Ankhorfall barrage entered the field from low orbit height. Master Fintha responded and seized battle sectors M-322a and M-322b. A total of 4 assault banners (Gray Wedge, Flood Peak, Blazing Fire, and Black Wings) were committed as reinforcements to assault the Ankhorfall sites. 
(COMMENT: I must reiterate that issues stemming from our understrength field combat and early warning formations have become significant. Our assault banners should not be committed in such low-intensity conflicts. The Order is facing a worsening situation. We must introduce new detection measures, or train casters skilled in the Arts of detection and scrying and include them within our banners.) 
MAIN ENGAGEMENT: 
1600 hours, February 11: The battle escalated as the termination of the Ankhors occurred behind schedule. 
0100 hours, February 12: Sudden spike in Aggeloid spawning rates reported. Incoming bombardments forced us to retract the radius of anti-air coverage and impeded the transport of our reserves. Sightings of an unregistered Aggeloid pattern (temporarily codenamed "High Tower" by our frontline elements) were also confirmed. The assault banner Gray Wedge engaged the High Tower ahead of schedule, causing our frontal attack formations to disintegrate one after another. Contact with assault banners Flood Peak and Blazing Fire was lost. Preemptive tactical Ankhor strikes failed. Battlefield dynamics shifted to artillery duels and defense consolidation on both sides. 
1800 hours, February 13: Contact with assault banner Black Wings was lost. Battlefield dynamics have entered a complete stalemate. 
2100 hours, February 15: Numerous giant Aggeloi breached battle sector M-322a. Contact with assault banner Gray Wedge was lost. 
(COMMENT: We have an official codename for the unregistered Aggeloid pattern: Psithyrosson) 
ENDGAME: 
0800 hours, February 16: Mothership from the 6th Standard arrived at the field, providing the required reinforcements for securing air superiority. Effectiveness of our artillery formations was re-established. Master Grimnir deployed 15 banners of foot and artillery that successfully arrived in battle sector M-320a. 
2300 hours, February 18: All Ankhors eliminated. About 80% of the Aggeloi were neutralized. The remnants withdrew to the areas beyond the Aurora circle. Pursuit was no longer possible. 
For this battle, our two standards report a loss of 623 killed and 854 severely wounded. Our carrier mothership was forced to return to port for major repairs. Heavy losses were suffered by the foot banners Stone Claws, Weregild, and Thorned Razors. These banners have since been merged and re-organized. Assault banners Flood Peak, Blazing Fire, and Black Wings have been removed from our roster. One Oathkeeper, though no longer combat-capable, remains in the assault banner Gray Wedge. Pursuant to a signed directive from the Castellan, the understrength banner shall continue their crusade in our rear. 
(COMMENT: The Commandery has always respected the judgment of the frontlines. Nevertheless, the details of the concluding section were unnecessary. If you insist on defending that Oathkeeper of that assault banner, then I shall provide a more detailed analysis report regarding the Psithyrosson. Truth be told, I am not inclined to believe our best elites would commit an error as severe and inane as in this particular case. Also, given the limited intel we have so far, I have my doubts and suspicions about whether that entity can be classified as an Aggelos, if at all... In any case, I will do whatever is necessary, to the greatest extents permitted by our principles of justice and fairness.) 
This concludes our current understanding of the event. The Castellan awaits your reply. 

(COMMENT: My opinion has been furnished throughout this report. The original shall be mailed to you directly. Note that the Grand Archives is extremely concerned with the sudden pike in Aggeloid spawning rates. Your performances in this battle were less than ideal. Perhaps a face-to-face meeting can be arranged soon enough.)

Operator Chen Qianyu was a native of Hongshan City and once served at the Wuling Scientific Developmental District. Supervisor Perlica later recruited her, via a private channel, to Endfield Industries. She is now a core member of the Crisis Team. Given her outstanding capabilities and mobility, Operator Chen Qianyu is an indispensable component of the Team. 

Those seeking to join Endfield have demonstrated a wide range of literary skills when describing their motives. However, the HR Division has yet to establish basic standards for reviewing the [Personal Motivations] section. If this section were completed in a manner that is too curt and/or straightforward, I will ask the operator to re-write their motivations in a style that they are comfortable with. However, despite being given five standard days to revise this section, Operator Chen Qianyu still persisted in writing: "I just wanna join. It's fate." Reading this, I realized the need to reflect upon our current review standards and establish a new framework, while paying extra attention to the two blades that Operator Chen Qianyu placed on my table (though she claimed that she did not do so to threaten me). 
Operator Chen Qianyu's inner thoughts and feelings are not as casual as she makes them out to be. Taking into consideration of her relatively rich past experiences, it is obvious that the extremely brief and terse description of her personal motives was a conclusion she arrived at after an extended period of self-contemplation. 
Additionally, I also realized that Operator Chen Qianyu's recruitment has been specifically approved by Supervisor Perlica. From my readings, the recent years have been a period where our Supervisor exhibited emotional fluctuations. The operator managed to solve many potential issues by offering much needed stability and support. 
Most importantly, I may have neglected how the simple line: "I just wanna join. It's fate." is actually congruent to the inner logic of the Endfield strategic objectives. In other words, these words could be seen as an alternate interpretation of the "Unity in Purpose" approach in partnership espoused by our Endministrator, which I also have in my records. Perhaps we now have an explanation capable of satisfying all parties involved in this review. 
— Martin Marvin Malen, Assistant, HR Division, Endfield Industries

The sun had yet to rise.
The warrior of the Coldpine Tribe was already awake. His hand held a short charcoal pen and the paper beneath it was barely larger than his palm.
Every space counted, for there was a lot that he wanted to write. He scratched the words carefully and read every word out loud. Though he tried to keep his voice low, the one next to him stirred. The woman opened her remaining eye, gave him a vicious kick and a cold rasp: "Quiet."
The warrior gave her a foolish smile, then started reciting his writings silently in his mind: "Dear Mamma, the ice has melted and we could see the green mosses. They feel good. They look lovely. I believe spring has arrived at your place. The river must be flowing beneath your treehouse and giving water to the plants in the garden. The fowls have probably returned to roost beneath the roof, fluttering into the house when you open the window so they can rest in your hand. Perhaps a day will come when I can fly home to you like the fowls, and stay by your side where spring is eternal, and..."
It was a word that his mother often spoke of. The warrior remembered it but forgot how it was shaped. Left with no choice, he stopped writing and gave the woman a look of resignation and a sincere need for help.
The woman's annoyed words did not hide an undertone of curiosity: "Why stop writing?"
"There's a word, but I can't shape it."
"And what is that word?"
"Sa-Sanctuary."
"You never learned it?"
"Mamma left me before she taught me the word."
"Ooooooh," the woman dragged it out as though frustrated. She then raised her hand and drew it in the air, a criss-crossing pattern of curved arcs and straight lines, like the mid-air trails left by a darting fowl.
The woman wrote out the word quickly at first. The warrior's tired eyes could barely keep track of her fingertip. She saw his knotted brows and chuckled, and then wrote the word out again.
Together, the warrior's charcoal pen, the woman's finger, the lines on the paper, and the shape in the air formed the word. It came together like a fowl making a slow landing on the ground.
The paper was now full of words. He gave a satisfied smile and then chucked it into the campfire. It crackled as it burned, and the firelight danced in the woman's eye before spluttering out at the corner of her gaze.
"You believe this would never reach her?"
The warrior nodded. The woman let out a sigh. There was a moment of silence before she suddenly spoke again. "What is your name, child?"
"Björn, of the Coldpines."
The woman reminisced as she voiced out her memories, one fragment at a time: "The Coldpine Tribe... Oh yes, I remember your Chieftain... A brave warrior, and very admirable. She honored the warrior's creed when she fell."
"I am fortunate, for I grew up with her," the warrior's face was flushed as he nodded at her with gratitude.
"May she return to Sami's side, a place of eternal spring, the..."
"The Sanctuary," the warrior said the word together with the woman as she smiled.
The sun had yet to rise, but the horns were trumpeting. The Aggeloi appeared at the horizon, marching towards the frontlines as a mighty host.
The Coldpine warrior was already on his feet. He took up the spear and carried the woman. Together with the soldiers, he turned to face the Aggeloid tide.
Behind them, the fires consumed the paper. Stray embers flew out of flickering tongues and floated to a faraway place.

DOCUMENT: A certain log that requires sufficient authority level 
According to reports by members of Operations Team Z7, Antal is exceptionally skilled in Originium Arts. His ability to cast the Arts far exceeds that of other operators in his cohort. When conducting a certain operation, Op Team Z7 members witnessed how Antal, in a crucial moment, positioned himself before the hostage. The operator used his Originium Arts to instantly disintegrate the greatsword swung by the attacking Landbreaker, and saved both himself and the hostage. 
It was an extremely intense moment. Antal would immediately lose his life if he failed to de-weaponize the attacker. However, he himself remained extremely calm throughout the entire incident. Since then, members of Op Team Z7 gained a deeper appreciation of Antal's abilities — Though he was known for being slow when it comes to sensing dangers in the environment or picking up changes in the emotions of other people, he was willing to risk his own life to save others. This revealed Operator Antal to be an extremely kind and courageous individual. 
Antal was remarkably humble when his teammates asked him about what he did. Antal replied that he did not perfectly wield his Originium Arts and failed to achieve his grandmother's level of expertise. He claimed the old lady could take apart and reassemble large metal machinery, while disintegrating a Landbreaker's weapon was the most he could do. Antal also mentioned that his grandmother crafted a small staff for him during his childhood to make up for his lack of power. 
"Your talent lies elsewhere — That is what my grandmother told me. And I have absolutely faith in her words."

Thank you for visiting my humble abode. Please, take a seat. Apologies for being unable to greet you on my two feet. Ah, just a fracture of the calf bones. I'll be out of the plaster next month. It's healing nicely and I don't think anything worse could happen. 
I'm more than happy to support your investigation. But really, this is just a minor issue of being bested by my betters, to put it simply... Oh yes, there's no personal grudges or disagreements between the two of us. I formally submitted my application to her and took part in the "trials" as agreed. Now, I'd never met Lady Azrila. However, it was an opportunity for joining the Order of Steel Oath and their legendary banners. If you've read anything about their crusading traditions, and if you're the type of person who wants to defend the homes of your people, no warrior would ever let this opportunity slip by. Pardon my insolence, but what actually makes you think this is an issue of personal grudges? 
...She didn't pass anyone? Not even that champion knight from the majors? Is that so? That's a little different from what I've been told. Regardless, I do not agree with your guesses. People can indeed communicate with each other by crossing their blades, and our blades did cross. Let me think... Oh, something small did happen afterwards. I hope it'll help you decide what really happened. 
Lady Azrila actually paid me a visit after the "trials". I sensed there was something on her mind, and I was concerned she felt guilty for not stopping her sword in time and accidentally hurting me. So that was what I asked, but she just smiled apologetically and countered with a question of her own: "Was there any time when you felt helpless?" 
Honestly, I felt helpless in more occasions than I could ever hope for. But given the circumstances and vibe of our conversation, I believe that we were not talking about the same thing. 
"The powerful enemy is before you, but you no longer had the strength to even swing your blade. Your comrades are slowly losing every hope of victory just to keep you alive... What would you do in this situation? Or rather, what would you let them do?" 
I have no idea why she asked me this question or what she hoped to get out of it. I just gave her my honest answer: "I would hate to admit this, but if I'm already a piece of dead weight, I might as well give my comrades another chance. We can't afford to suffer any defeats. The Civilization Band is right behind us." 
I was trying to join the Order of Steel Oath and it was natural for me to read about the stories from the frontlines. But ... she looked really conflicted after listening to my answer. "Nilla and Claire did exactly that," she said, "They all did... And this is why I cannot approve you." 
Blightery, that was the first time my brain ever overclocked itself. I had a feeling that she did not outright disagree with me. She seemed to be hesitating about other things... No. I don't really care about passing or failing her trials. I just want to help. It was during this time that Lady Azrila seemed as though she was ... in need of serious help. 
So, I did my best to think about all sorts of possibilities and acted as though I know what actually happened. I told her, "If you're seeking revenge on an enemy, just remember that nobody wants their friend to die trying to avenge them." 
...Yeah, even I felt it was a dumb thing to say and I immediately regretted my words. Then we said absolutely nothing for about five minutes or so. But Lady Azrila was actually really friendly. She forced herself to smile and comforted me by praising my combat skills. She even told me I could seek the others out and try again after my wounds heal. 
And after that, we talked a little bit more before she left... Oh, before I forget, she also asked me plenty of things about you. Since you're here specifically to ask me all these questions, does that mean she's going to stay at Endfield Industries for a while? 

(NOTES: This is followed by friendly banter that does not require specific review. Also, we advise getting the logistics operators ready. Operator Ember may need to receive an ordinary visitor next month.)

DOCUMENT: Endfield Industries Medical Division Service Log 
AUTHOR: Dulla Gray, clinical psychologist 

LOG 1 
Surgeon Answorth has been dispatched to the surface in response to an emergency. So, this is my first time providing psychotherapeutic services on my own ever since I joined Endfield. The details of the job is to provide psychological evaluations for an onboarding operator. I hope this is the start of a beautiful relationship between us. 
............ 
I've waited for six hours but the operator did not show up. 

LOG 2 
I verified the records. Turns out the operator is a reconvener troubled by "polymnestic disorders". I remain the chief therapist in charge of this case. 
My second meeting (which is technically the first, all facts considered) with Operator Laevatain was successful. I did the psychological evaluations that we missed last time, and she also explained why she failed to show up for that meeting. It appeared that she was deeply troubled and annoyed by certain nightmares. Hence, she chose to head to the surface and "sort the feelings out". With my encouragement, she agreed to describe her dreams to me. 

Laevatain dreamed of herself standing in a classroom. One by one her classmates introduced themselves on the stage. But when it was her turn, she tried to open her mouth but no voice came out. She tried again, but her throat began to hurt and she only managed to emit blurred, raspy noises. 
The teacher turned around, but a raging flame danced where her face should be, "You could not say it because you never had your own life." 
Laevatain tried to leave the classroom, only to find herself in a familiar yet alien-looking house. Everything around her was burning. The fire consumed the walls, the books, and the mirrors. Her classmates, friends, teachers, families, and even colleagues she met in Rhodes Island and Dijiang stood in the room, but all their faces were contortions of twisted flame and no longer recognizable. 
She then ran for the door and forced her way through, only to find herself in the exact same house, also on fire. She ran again, opened the door, and saw the same thing. 
With every door she went through, the room got smaller and the flames got closer. 
In the end, she opened the final door and arrived at a room of ashes with neither fire nor smoke. She saw herself seated in the room, smiling at her: 
"You finally burnt everything." 

Laevatain's recurring dream appears to be rooted in "memories" she has carried in her mind. Whether these are drawn from real experiences or mere illusions is unclear, but it seems she has been journeying with this burden for a long time. 

LOG 3 
I tried prescribing several recommended therapies for Operator Laevatain but the results were less than ideal. After receiving suggestions from Surgeon Answorth, I asked Laevatain if she ever considered medical removal of these memories as the scenes and nightmares continue to affect her in an unabated fashion. 
She pondered for a moment and denied this advice. 
Several days later, she described another dream to me. 

In this dream, Laevatain woke up in a white world. The sky was clean and flawless, and the land seemed endless. 
She walked for a long time without feeling the wind. She met no one, heard nothing, and saw no shadows. 
A door stood at the very end. Posted on the door was a note — Enter, if you do not wish to be anyone else. 
There she stopped. She chose not to open the door. 

When the session ended, Operator Laevatain gave me a bunch of fiery red flowers — a token of gratitude for "future sessions of memory-sharing".

DOCUMENT: Combat Adaptation Test Records (ID: L-067) 
CANDIDATE: Laevatain (reconvener) 
MONITOR: Krad (Endfield Security Professional) 
OS: S7 Combat Simulation System 
CONTENTS: Mass suppression and precision strikes 
DURATION: 3 minutes 42 seconds 
RESULTS: Pass (conditional) 

TEST SUMMARY 
At the 7th second of Phase 1, Operator Laevatain summons a giant flaming blade with one hand (no equipment ID identified; said blade is likely created by Laevatain's Originium Arts) and charges directly into the center of the simulated enemy group before verbal instructions were given nor confirmed. 
At the 31st second, thermal readings exceeded simulation environment monitoring thresholds. System automatically activates anti-heat measures. Security Professional Krad requests to stop the test but Operator Laevatain denies the request. 
At the 1-minute and 24-second mark, Operator Laevatain had destroyed all enemy units and assumed a standing pose in the center of the simulation area, while adjusting her breathing after a high-intensity burst of activities. 
Combat resumed after 38 seconds to initiate Phase 2. Test item "Stationery Suppression" was initiated. The operator's performance was far more extreme than Phase 1 and the entire test was completed after 1 minute and 40 seconds. 

BEHAVIORAL SUMMARY 
Combat style is highly aggressive and prioritizes breaking the stalemate with overwhelming force. 
Prefers seizing combat initiative instead of focusing on tactical coordination. Willingness to support teamwork is unstable. 
Weapon efficacy is significantly improved at emotional thresholds. Effects include spreading fire, localized scorch marks, and signal interference. 

TEST REVIEW 
She is incredibly powerful but has yet to build up the mental fortitude to master it. She does not enjoy destruction, but uses combat as a means to vent her emotions and prove her existence. She must learn how to restrain herself and bring that instability under control — master the fire, but don't become the fire. If she loses her connection to medic or support operators in the team, no one would be able to save her. 
— Evaluations by Krad, Security Professional 

I don't think you gave me this test to see if I can still fight. You wanted to know if I would "lose control", right? Don't worry ... I know exactly what I'm doing. 
— Comments from Operator Laevatain 

NOTE: New thermal insulation must be installed in the combat testing area. If there is another test, also prepare 3 servings of Coolant Beverages. 

DOCUMENT: Post-Operational Summary (ID: SU-58R-TR) 
During this combat operation, Operator Laevatain charged into the enemy on her own accords at the initial stages of battle, and did not respond to tactical calls from her team. Her actions temporarily severed communications, disrupted the chain of command, and caused momentary panic amongst team members. Fortunately, the team did not suffer any casualties. 
When the operation ended, analyses of residual energy traces and tactical dataloggers confirmed that Operator Laevatain successfully diverted the focus of enemy fire toward herself with these means: deliberate exposure of her own position and continuous emission of super hot flames that disrupt enemy defenses. In other words, she used herself as a lure to create a tactical breach and allowed our attacking operators to exploit the opening and achieve our tactical objectives. 
Upon concluding the operation, Operator Laevatain sat on a cooled fragment of molten rock. Burn marks in the vicinity suggested that this area was subjected to extremely intensive strikes. Laevatain said nothing as we surveyed the battlefield. After ascertaining that all other operators were well, she softly said, "Good."

Other operators aboard the Dijiang often say that Supervisor Perlica seems to possess a kind of magical quality. As long as she's around, any problem finds its solution. 
So when I learned that I'd have the privilege of studying alongside her, I was so excited I couldn't sleep. But reality hit me hard. Unable to keep up with her intense workload and exacting standards, I seriously considered quitting along the way … yet I couldn't bring myself to give up such a precious opportunity. 
With the expected awakening of the Endministrator just around the corner, everyone is on edge—even Supervisor Perlica is no exception. Despite her schedule being completely packed, she still manages to squeeze in meetings with senior members from every department to ensure everything goes off without a hitch. 
But after each of those impromptu private meetings, she always comes out looking uneasy. Could it be that there are things even she can't handle? I can't help but blame myself for not being able to do more to help. 
She noticed how lost I felt and took the initiative to comfort me, even sharing some strangely flavored fin meatballs I'd never seen before. The taste was so strong it brought tears to my eyes, yet Supervisor Perlica just watched me with a satisfied smile … That day's worries were washed away along with my tears. 
In that moment, I suddenly realized that Supervisor Perlica … truly does have that kind of magic. 
—From the work log of a trainee operator, who is still applying for the opportunity to continue her apprenticeship under Supervisor Perlica. 

[Record That Has Not Been Successfully Deleted] 
"She went to see you too, didn't she, Krad? Asking how to get along with the Endministrator she cares about so much, right?" 
"Wouldn't expect anything less from Intel. You're not even on the Dijiang and you're still this well-informed. When she rushed into the training room to find me, I thought something had gone wrong. But then she asked me that dead seriously. Totally took me by surprise." 
"Guess I've gotten so used to her being the Supervisor that I almost forgot she isn't actually invincible. But I do love that awkward tone she takes when she messages me. Still just as adorable as when we were kids." 
"So, what advice did you give her?"

"But I bet she'll hide it perfectly when she sees the Endministrator again."

"Relax, Krad. You know I am the last person to talk. Professional ethics and all. But honestly, it's almost a shame we won't get to see little Perlica pouting over this, isn't it?"

[Graduation Speech] 
"Hmmm... Greetings, everyone. I am Zhuang Fangyi from the Class of ██. It is truly an honor to stand here today on behalf of my fellow graduates. 
"I'm the youngest amongst you. Even fellow students who just enrolled are two years ahead of me. So I'd like to begin by thanking everyone for your care and support throughout these years. 
"Thank you for helping me reach the top shelves when I couldn't. Thank you for always saving me a front-row seat for the lectures. Thank you for holding back your frustration even when experiments stalled... 
"Most of all, although everyone spoiled me with loving exceptions usually reserved to a younger sibling, none of my ideas or suggestions were ever brushed off as childish. I skipped many years in school and lost the chance to befriend peers of my age. But in return, I gained invaluable friendships with those older than me. I missed out on one kind of companionship, but received guidance, mentorship, and trust from another. 
"Now, my next step is to continue my studies at the Hongshan Academy of Sciences. The colleagues I meet there are likely to be even more experienced... I also hope to learn from them and build new friendships..." 

[Eulogy] 
"I am keenly aware that many among you are far more suited than I to stand here today and deliver this eulogy for those we have lost. In the presence of parents, sons and daughters, lifelong companions, and loved ones ... I am but a mere youth. 
"I was the youngest member at the Science Station. The reason I could convey our longing on behalf of everyone is a result of your patience, guidance, and care... 
"I have made a journey blessed with support from all sides. I often asked my experienced peers how I might repay the trust and sincerity they showed me. They would always smile and tell me that doing my work and honoring the expectations placed upon me were the best means of repayment. 
"Though they are no longer with us, the trust they invested in me has not waned, nor has their faith in the Xiranite project. I understand that this is the moment to repay them in full... 
"And faithfully I shall bear those hopes and expectations upon my shoulders." 

Orientation Speech 
"Greetings, everyone. It is a great honor to welcome you to Wuling, where you have chosen to commit your most beautiful years to the laboratories, to this place, and to the forefront of our fight against the Blight and the Rift. 
"I know many of you chose Wuling because your parents and elders who sacrificed everything for the Science Station... Seeing your young, eager faces brings back memories — I sat where you are seated right now, and listened to your parents and elders who led me onto this path. 
"I once thought their greatest gift to me was the scientific achievements they had spent their lives creating. Now I realize the gift includes you who arrived at Wuling — who answered their call to follow their footsteps. 
"I once believed that the best way to honor their memories was to stay on that path and reach, without hesitation, the ideal future they dreamed of. Now I understand that I must also lead those who follow, to guide them onto that path and help them envision the future... 
"Thank you. 
"Thank you for choosing to walk this path with me."

DOCUMENT: Yvonne's work diary 
Day 3 after starting at that particular data section of the Æther rift. I can't see anything inside. All monitoring modules were knocked out. IR, EM, resonance responses — we got flatlined for everything. Not a single blip showed up. Sheesh. 
I tried to "read" the changes of that particular area with a smart sign language interpreter! And all I got was a bunch of errors and a single line that reads: "Failed to interpret data." 
We didn't just fail to monitor the stuff. The Æther rubbed it in our faces. We're completely blind to it. The only thing I'm certain of is this: It exists, and it's not very nice. 
I HATE THINGS I CAN'T SEE! 
............ 
Maybe I can change my approach. What would happen if I actively send data into it? Instead of just passively waiting for a response to come out of the output port, we should seize the initiative and interact with it instead. 
I tried three signal packs with different frequencies: (1) a standard greetings protocol; (2) a set of greetings I wrote myself in pulse-based format; (3) a set of static noise (the first note from the Movement: Genesis of the Universe, the Ætherside might like it). 
The results are just as predicted ... no responses. Fine. Be optimistic. Perhaps there was a response but receiving a radio wave transmission and emitting a response might take a while. If a single vibration takes at least 10 million years, then I have no choice but to keep Frost-e-Bytee on the receiving line. 
Perhaps I can try optical wave signals with various color codes. If that thing can see things, perhaps it'll like glittering stuff, like me! 
Plus light travels faster than sound! 
............ 
How many times did I fail again? Can't remember. Signal modulation, model simulations, and feedback monitoring ... none of it worked. The noise I'm getting sounds like the Æther laughing at me — I really hope it was laughing at me, because that means I'll unleash Frost-e-Bytee and ram some icy cold down its throat! 
I always believed that persistence will eventually identify a crack. But now I am beginning to wonder if this is a futile effort of exploration with no way out. 
We can't even "observe" this thing. How are we supposed to "decipher" it? 
The models I proposed and the devices I designed felt like childish gimmicks when compared to the Blight... 
............ 
Maybe the only thing I can do right now is to spin around on my swivel chair. Perhaps I gotta wait 10 million years for a miracle to happen. 
I might as well change my scientific approach. Time to build an invincible space armada. Let the ancient songs echo as I raise countless ... cities into the skies! Unfeasible? Maybe. But what can be more unfeasible than deciphering the Æther? 
I looked at those images of the Æther rift. I gazed at them long and hard. It devoured both sound and light. Even I got trapped within it — it crushed me and smothered me with eternal darkness. There is no escape for me. 
So why am I doing all this? To protect Talos-II...? To prove myself...? Because I got a grudge against Pa and Ma...? No. I think it all started on that day. I read about the Æther rift in the books and found it beautiful. So I snuck off to the Protection Band so I could observe it, like the giddy girl I was. The rift gave off a bright halo. Looking at it feels like staring straight into the sun. The piercing pain then gave way to a sense of indescribable horror and then it ... melted. 
It was a terror that got me bawling and trembling under my blankets late that night. My eyes swelled like peaches in the following morning — I looked gross. And I don't ever want to look like that again. So that's it: I'm going to decipher it. It's as simple as that. 
And I believe I can do it at Endfield. 
So once again, I punched the [SEND] button. A resounding KABLAM of epic proportions and ZERO hesitation. Gone and dusted. The darkness will be no more, and I shall return to daytime.

Three tolls of the bell sounded. One by one, the people at the gathering removed their hats and stepped forward to place fresh flowers into the cold coffin.
Some wept quietly, others bowed their heads in silence. Rozzan scanned the surroundings, but he didn't spot that familiar crimson figure anywhere.
The last of the Elder Wolves who survived the incident laid in the casket. He spent the rest of his days in pain. Though the Bonekrusher's haze ravaged his organs and their blades pierced his limbs, the Elder Wolf held on tightly to the swaddled young pup ... until he passed her into the arms of another boy...
"She's still not here..."
The words reached Rozzan. He gave a slow nod, then quietly passed the rest of the service over to another Elder.
He knew where to find her. Whenever she was upset, she'd lose herself in the training grounds and stay there until late into the night.
Rozzan watched the girl in silence. She noticed him too, but neither said a word. With one last fierce thrust, she drove her sword into the training dummy and collapsed to the ground. No one knew how long she had been pushing herself here.
"He's gone."
Rozzan approached Rossi where she lay gasping on the ground, his voice quiet and flat.
"I know... I know..."
Rossi pulled her hood down over her eyes, but her voice shook uncontrollably. Ever since she was old enough to understand, she had visited the wounded Old Wolf every single week so he could see that she was growing up strong and well. To her, he was the last living thread connecting her to those lost souls.
"You should have been there. He would have wanted you there."
"But ... it was because of me... He did it all for..."
Rozzan hoisted her up and slung her over his shoulder before she could finish, carrying her toward the courtyard where the funeral was being held.
"I can't face him ... it was all my fault... I don't want to..."
Rossi thrashed and bit against Rozzan's shoulder. Her nails scraped his skin, her teeth sank into his arm. Rozzan's expression didn't flicker. He just kept walking toward the funeral.
Soon, Rossi's strength gave out. She slumped against Rozzan's back, arms hanging limp.
"I didn't become the wolf the Pack could rely on..."
Rossi murmured, unsure if she was speaking to Rozzan, or to someone no longer there.
"I never learned to stand on my own. I couldn't lead anyone. I haven't done a single thing right... I didn't deserve their sacrifice..."
Rozzan came to a stop. The courtyard was empty now, save for the ashes of burnt offerings and a solitary coffin. Inside, the elder lay peacefully, covered in flowers.
"Every time you came to see him, he'd always pull me aside afterward to talk. Maybe age caught up to the wolf and he never remembered what he told me. Just kept ranting the same stories on and on."
Rozzan set Rossi down. He rested a hand on the edge of the coffin, gazing at his old friend.
"He'd always go on about the glory days, the few times we butted heads. But the details ... those kept changing. One day he was the one who messed up, the next it was me. The same story was told different every time. Only one thing he ever said never changed."
Rozzan reached over and ruffled Rossi's hair.
"Every single time, he'd say that saving you was the greatest thing he ever did."
Rossi lowered her head. She took off the pale pendant from around her neck, the one the elder had given her, and placed it among the flowers.
The coffin sealed. The young wolf never cried again.

After the fall of Sami, most of the Sami people accepted the outcome. They live atop the Feranmut's remains, carrying on His will, fighting the Aggelos to protect Talos-II.
Yet there were still Snowpriests who believed that Sami had not truly died. His soul had merely been lost within the rifts, fallen into a deep slumber. One day, Sami would wake from His dream and return to His people. They traveled to the rifts across Talos-II, setting up altars and performing rituals, trying to call Sami's soul back from the fissures. But none who went ever returned. Later, with the northern front growing ever more urgent, no one was willing to continue the attempt.
In a snowy forest near the Wuling Very Large Rift, Typhoeus found the manuscripts left behind by one of those Sami Snowpriests. The manuscripts detailed all her attempts to awaken Sami. Though Typhoeus was able to confirm through her own exploration that the ritual had failed and the Snowpriestess had vanished without a trace, the girl still caught a faint whiff of possibility from the remaining materials.
Unfortunately, after months of study, Typhoeus had made no progress.
She asked every Snowpriest and shaman in the Order of Steel Oath and Myrkwood, but they all just shook their heads, believing it to be a doomed endeavor.
Even after hitting so many dead ends, Typhoeus did not lose heart. The Snowpriestess's unique insights on dreams in the manuscripts taught the girl to perceive special revelations within the dreamscapes of others.

"I don't know why, but lately I keep dreaming of being chased by a gigantic monster. The ground beneath my feet keeps swaying, as if I am standing on a suspension bridge. I toss and turn all night long..."
"Simple. That monster is hunting you, and you have been cornered."
"What should I do?"
"Become stronger. Do not be the prey. Be the hunter instead."
"I think I get it now."

After that conversation with Typhoeus, the operator mapped out a full month of intensive training for himself. The exhaustion and sense of accomplishment from the workouts let him sleep soundly through the night. Before long, Endfield colleagues began showing up at Typhoeus's door with all sorts of dreams, asking her to read and interpret them.
And Typhoeus, after listening to everyone's dreams, drew inspiration from them to craft a legend of her own, one that wove together the Feranmut Sami, dreams, and the Snowpriests.
Soon, Typhoeus finished writing the ending. She thought the matter would settle just like the story itself. So she gathered her notes and set off to share the conclusion with those who had been waiting eagerly. But halfway there, she brushed past a young girl in the corridor.
Typhoeus did not recognize her, yet she felt a strangely familiar presence emanating from her.
It was a presence that had accompanied her people through swamps and forests, through winters and into springs, from birth all the way to death.
By the time Typhoeus came to her senses, the girl had already walked far away.
Later, she learned from others the girl's codename: Last Rite.
Driven by a mysterious premonition, she tore out the ending she had written and wrote that codename on a fresh page instead.

"Endfield is a legitimate enterprise. You need to learn to distinguish fact from rumor. Not all those legends are true."
Every time a new employee joins Endfield, the veteran staff makes a point of reminding them of this.
That was until Operator Typhoeus joined Endfield, and all that effort went down the drain. With her rambling, mystical tales, this girl blurred the line between rumor and reality, turning us from a company with a certain legendary flair into ... a legend, plain and simple.
The mysterious characters flashing across the screens, the crying sounds echoing from the bridge late at night, the lighting fixtures in the Engineering Division that never seem to stay fixed, always flickering on and off when someone is alone. These little coincidences, easily dismissed with a laugh, were gathered and woven together by Typhoeus into a spine-chilling legend.

Long ago, the equipment aboard the sky vessel Dijiang was constantly breaking down. The poor craftsmen had no choice but to take shelter in the workshop, forging and repairing day and night without rest. Yet after a full year of toil, the number of machines awaiting repair only grew, piling up around them like an unbroken mountain range.
Consumed by rage, his last shred of kindness was spent. He transformed into a vengeful spirit and entered the machinery itself, vowing to take revenge on every careless soul who cut corners in their operations.
The lights flickering in the night are the sign of his patrol.
— An entry from Typhoeus's notebook.

After this story spread across Dijiang, the number of damage reports on the Engineering Division's repair list for that month dropped significantly.
After looking into the matter, the stunned Mr. Andre gave a fair assessment of the story: this was not a story, but an indisputable fact.
And this was just one chapter among the many legends Typhoeus had written for Endfield. In her notebook, the Endministrator was the great sage holding the Stone of Origin, Supervisor Perlica was the lightning mage wielding the power of thunder, Miss Chen was a ranger carrying a longsword. And everything Endfield did on Talos-II was planting great stone swords across the land to maintain peace in the world and protect all living things.
A twelve-year-old child would find these tales childish, but for the Endfield operators with their heads full of whimsy, they were just right.
"When I am working now, I imagine myself as a mysterious Sami Snowpriest. When the equipment overheats, I shout out ancient invocations..." And with that, Andre picked up the cooling gun from the corner, aimed it at the machine, and cried out, "O wind and snow, descend upon the mortal world!"

Before, reflecting on the past used to come naturally for Shiba Momiji. Back in school, she had a knack for breaking down a year's worth of progress with neat charts and detailed annotations — earning top grades with ease. 
But now, things are different. It's been a full year since Operations Team Z7 was formed. And instead of stats and milestones, what fills her heart now ... are feelings. 
She constantly worries about Catcher. As the team's shield and support, he looks after everyone like family. Is he overextending himself...? 
She pays attention to Estella's condition. Some may see her as unmotivated or laid-back, but Akekuri knows better. Estella is healing her own fragile body while quietly helping Op Z7 heal the world. That takes a rare kind of strength. 
She watches over Fluorite's moods, not just her frequent outbursts or headstrong ways. Akekuri often asks herself: Am I being a strong enough cushion? One that lets her feel understood and safe? 
She worries about Antal too. Often labeled an "odd one," Antal is, in truth, passionate and reliable — his way of connecting simply different. She sees how hard he's been working to keep pace with the team. 
It's because of them that Z7 stands as it does today. 
She's deeply grateful — for their trust, for their belief in her leadership, and for proving that this team, once seen as inexperienced, could stand on its own. 
But most of all, she wonders about herself: Has she met the expectations she set — using what little they had to help as many as possible ... and to find her own light in the process? 
Sometimes she wonders: if the ideals of Endfield are ever fulfilled, and peace finally comes — maybe, just maybe, her parents might reconcile. And perhaps she could go home, just like when she was little ... and share one peaceful family meal together again. 
She is giving her all to make that future possible. 

Annual Performance Report
SUBMITTED BY: Akekuri, Captain, Operations Team Z7 

Dear Supervisor Perlica, 
This report outlines the major operations and achievements of Operations Team Z7 over the past year. 
We completed 40 missions with a 95% success rate and zero casualties. These included 16 cross-region supply runs, 9 joint wildlands recon operations, 7 high-risk engineering escorts, and 8 emergency rescues. 
We've steadily grown from a provisional support force into a reliable, fully operational unit. 
P.S. While our combat rating remains average in this year's assessment, we ranked among the top in support, command, and management. 
......
Regarding the rumored awakening of the "Endministrator," though I have yet to witness it myself, I can feel the excitement in  stories shared by our seniors. If possible, I'd like to respectfully request that Operations Team Z7 be involved in missions under the Endministrator's command. It would be a privilege to personally deliver our tactical reports — and even more meaningful to work alongside the Endministrator to bring Endfield's vision to life. Together, we can restore peace to Talos-II...

Regular Work Report for Operators Under the Endministrator 
REPORTED BY: Laevatain 

I escorted the messenger to this volcanic basin. Molten lava flowed through the ground beneath our feet, heating the rain and creek, causing the earth to froth and bubble endlessly. The monitoring station stood right atop this "cauldron of living soup". 
This place is extremely poor in Originium. Resident scientists rely on geothermal heat to cook food. A ration tin can be cooked through simply by burying it in the dirt for an hour. They even have "pocket stews": a liquid stock and other ingredients sealed in a food-grade bag — after quick cooking, you can just tear it open with your teeth. I got a face full of hot stew once, and it felt like I was on fire. 
When I had my first meal, the scientist taught me to sing their "ritual" chant: "May your soup never spill, and may your flame never die." 
I sang the chant with him. It was the first time I received a stranger's blessing on Talos-II. 
— Sent from Monitoring Station 34 

As the Operator closest to the incident and the most capable emergency responder, I was ordered to reach the UWST base not marked on the map with the greatest speed I could muster. 
The issue was not complicated. Just an unexpected blast furnace malfunction, shutdown, and loss of power. I spent a bit of my powers and helped them re-ignite the core. Temperature returned to operational levels and the system was restored. The crisis was temporarily averted. 
Their "names" left quite an impression on me. The place was a secret base in the frigid lands of █████, usually referred to by its unique beacon code. Everyone there was forbidden from using their real names or any self-chosen codenames; only the "assigned" name was allowed. 
My temporary name here was "Olga Randall". I was told there were three others before me with the same name, and it's likely that the next replacement actuary sent here will also take on this name. 
It was a strange experience. I was just a temporary user of the name "Olga Randall". It felt similar to the memory fragments swimming in my mind. Neither the name nor the fragments were truly mine, but at that very moment, they were all part of me. 
— Sent from UWST Beacon DAU.14 

After eliminating the Aggelos camping in the freight station, I reopened the gate that had kept the tunnel sealed for quite a while. 
They maintained a low gravity environment within the tunnels. Refugees, trapped here for months, floated their way to the exit, trembling and struggling as they left the place. They must relearn how to walk and run under the ponderous influence of gravity. 
But there was a little girl who floated within the tunnels and danced for a bit before leaving the place. She told me it was how she kept herself calm and sane when they were trapped in this place. 
I memorized her dance, a comforting yet powerful routine of rhythms. If you want, I can show it to you and let you have a go once I head back. The moves aren't hard. It's all about the breathing and the rhythms. 
— Sent from freight nexus MC-20 

I've made plenty of new memories during this time. I still remember that you're chasing after your own memories as well. I found a few places related to the old "you". Seek me out if you're interested. 
— Emergency message, sent from Contact Point 084A

In a time when most Landbreakers are seen as "destroyers of order", the Pack stands out as an anomaly. They value order and hold a peaceful attitude toward the Civilization Band. Even now, they cling to certain old traditions, such as strong familial bonds and a deep respect for unity. 
That very difference only fueled the long-standing feud between them and their rivals, the Bonekrushers. Over ten years ago, the Bonekrushers struck with a vicious ambush, shattering the Pack when they were at their weakest — just after the death of their Alpharion. 
Wulfgard and his younger sister survived the attack, but they refused to speak of what truly happened. 
Wulfgard then left the Pack a few years after his coming-of-age ceremony, keeping in touch with only a few trusted friends and his sister. 
No one ever knew why he left. He stayed silent, just like he did about the attack. 
Later, he approached Endfield and proposed a partnership. He eventually joined the Specialist Tech Division as an operator. 
Someone once asked why he chose Endfield. 
At first, he was silent. Then, with startling honesty, he answered: 
"I want another future for the Pack... and Endfield holds the possibility of making it real." 
Wulfgard spoke candidly of the Pack's struggles. His steady resolve and honest intent opened doors. 
So it made perfect sense when he became an operator. As he put it, he had a duty — to prove the Pack's worth and to repay Endfield's trust in him. 
Since then, he's become a quiet but reliable presence on many tough and dangerous missions. 
Operators who once held deep prejudice against the Landbreakers began to change their views — thanks to Wulfgard. 
Then, opinions shifted once more after the arrival of his sister — Operator Rossi. But that's a story for another time...

What do I think of the north? Worst place ever ... I swear! I seriously messed up agreeing to join Rooter on his hunt for that mysterious Sami vendor out in the middle of nowhere! We went over the first snowpeak and were barely two days into the north when some Blighted snowstorm "caught" us at the foot of the mountains! 
I will never forget the sight of an entire burdenbeast being swooshed away by the Blight-tainted snow. The only thing on my mind was: "Blasted blightery! I'm gonna die here..." 
But I guess I saved up enough luck for the past decade or so! The snowstorm was just meters away from us when an Ursus girl swooped in from the skies — I kid you not! She flew in on a snowboard, pulled off a perfect landing next to us, slammed a shield on the ground, and suddenly a wall of ice appeared with a WOOSH! That wall kept the snowstorm away! 
Anyway, she saved both Rooter and me. She escorted us into a cave that she called our temporary shelter. 
And there were all sorts of people there... Oathkeepers, Seš'qa caravan drivers, and even Landbreakers! 
I still remember how we just walked in and some tall and mean-looking Feline started pointing his finger at us, "These two! They're frauds plotting to bring their swindling ways to Sami! I heard all about their dirty plots along the way. Why are you saving these lowlives? Don't let them cheat you!" It was only then when I suddenly recognized the Feline. He was the guide who traveled with us a few days back... I had wondered why he suddenly returned the commission and refused to guide us any longer... 
Anyway, I thought we were finished but the Ursus lass who brought us in said nothing. She gave the Feline a glance and the big mean kittyboy ... just sat down and said nothing else. 
I wanted to thank her personally back then, but she soon rushed out to carry on with her SAR. I couldn't even get her name. Another SAR team soon arrived and brought us to safety. 
But I recognized the badges and markings on her outfit. They were the same as the illustrations in the shelter. 
What happened next...? Well, I found your place. That's what happened. Hah! Just take these supplies. My token of gratitude to that Ursus lass! 
— Recordings from a donor of the Northern Corridor Rescue Union

Antal was born in a normal household in the Free City of New Wrankwood. He spent most of his childhood growing up in a household Originium appliance repair shop belonging to his grandmother. 
Although Antal lived in a place known for its entertainment industry, he had no interest in the movies or performance industries. Instead, he preferred lying on the table and looking at his grandmother work — Her jobs include repairing a faulty refrigerator and swapping out its Originium starter component, or restoring a television with a shattered screen and severely damaged mainboard to mint conditions... The old repairlady had jobs everyday, but she never neglected her grandson. When she had time, she would personally design and make various toys such as mini sports cars and powered combo-puzzle cubes for the lad. Hence, Antal grew up very much loved and never felt lonely. Years of influence from his grandmother gave Antal an outstanding talent for assembling and taking apart Originium devices. He successfully secured a full scholarship in an academy and chose a major related to applications of Originium automation. 
The academy where Antal studied at was known for its conservative atmosphere. The youth, however, was not an adherent to the rules. When his novel inventions failed to acquire the favor of his professors, he chose to continue his project in private. For his academic excellence, Antal became the valedictorian for the graduation ceremony. He mounted his latest invention on his back — an automated Originium-powered robot arm, and enthusiastically used it to wave at the professors who once scoffed at the idea. And then suddenly, the open hand of the robot lowered four of its fingers, save for one that remained still and fully extended. 
Although the incident left quite a psychological trauma to members of the academy's administration, Antal was still able to graduate. Wulfgard knew better than anyone, that leaving the Pack for good meant this journey had no return date. By his own standards, that meant packing everything that might prove useful. 
Yet, standing before Il Cacciatore and sweeping his gaze over the massive rig that had been his and his sister's home for nearly a decade... he realized, abruptly, that there was nothing left worth taking. 
He went over his plans once more in his mind: make sure Rossi knew exactly who in the clan could be trusted, confirm the two ways people could reach him, ask Tommaso to keep a close watch over Rossi, settle the last bit of custom work fees at Uncle Rust's, feed Giovanni's semi-wild fowlbeasts one last time, entrust them to little Vincenzo next door... No, he hasn't forgotten a thing. 
Satisfied, he turned for one final check. Just to be absolutely sure he hadn’t left Rossi's handmade Originium lamp glowing on the bedside table. 
But as soon as he stepped into his sleeping compartment, his eyes caught sight of something in an unremarkable corner of the cabinet: his worn guns — the very first weapons he'd ever owned. 
Though secondhand and now running low on compatible ammo, those guns were priceless treasures back then. They kept him and his sister alive, earned him his first mercenary contract, and helped him take down his first target. When one of the Originium activators failed, he was forced to master one-handed reloads and gun maintenance. After three years of supporting his family with mercenary pay, he finally replaced the worn Originium activator and even crafted a set of custom-etched ammo. 
These guns were passed down from the clan's elders. Like many inherited dreams, they met their end during a high-stakes escort mission, overheating after prolonged firing. 
Soon after, Uncle Rust — a bounty hunter who had returned to the Pack and opened a weapon refurbishment shop called "Howlfire Gunsmiths." There, Wulfgard was introduced to custom weapon modifications for the first time. 
Then he learned to make weapons truly his own, even if they only suited him. 
Still, he never got rid of those guns that got him started. They remained tucked away in a quiet corner. 
Why keep them? As a reminder? A keepsake? Or a memento of painful memories? 
He wasn't sure — maybe all, maybe none. 
After confirming the Originium lamp was off, he headed for the door, ready to embark on a journey that might finally give him an answer.

With a flutter of crimson, she touched down bearing saccharine candies, animal-shaped origami, and a kaleidoscope of colored pencils. 
The kids swarmed around the mysterious Miss Messenger, who came by every now and then with treats, gifts, and tales they'd never heard before. 
Together, they drew her stories' vibrant fowlbeasts, then folded sugary foil into tiny mirrors of themselves. 
As the evening bell rang, she said goodbye to each kid, watching them run home. 
One girl tugged softly at Miss Messenger's skirt. She had nowhere to go. 
With a gentle touch to her head, the Messenger sent the girl floating upward as a startled yelp escaped her lips. 
Together, they watched the moon climb the night sky as stars arranged themselves into fleeting constellations. 
"Miss ... aren't you going home?" 
The girl whispered, lowering her head, knowing the Messenger would soon leave her. 
"My home... lies beyond the far horizons. Or should I say, it hides beyond the sky and behind the stars themselves." 
"Behind the stars?" 
"Would you like to visit?" 
The girl nodded, then shook her head. She ached to go, yet feared troubling her beloved Miss Messenger. 
"Don't worry. I've told my colleagues about a brilliant little girl. They all want to meet you too." 
"R-really?" 
"Uh-huh. I would never lie to you. Oh, wait, it's time." 
"It's ... time?" 
"Close your eyes and don't peek. In three ... two ... one ... Voila!" 
In Miss Messenger's hands appeared two cupcakes. 
"Woah..." 
"Hehe, today's your birthday, right? Of course I remembered! This one's just for you." 
The girl stared wide-eyed at the Messenger as she dipped her cream-coated finger into her mouth, beaming with a sweet smile. 
"I- I want to visit your home..." 
To her, this cupcake was a treasure beyond price, held carefully as fragile glass.
Now aboard the Dijiang, she studies tirelessly to become an official technician at the EF-ED. 
Whenever challenges arise, she takes a cupcake to the Bridge and gazes toward Talos-II. She finds herself drawing courage from that familiar crimson figure, always trailing a scent of sugar and resolve.

Ahem. Hello people. I'm the new candidate consultant for angling strategies and instructor for hobby angling... Never heard of it? Ah. Yeah, I think some boss man prolly misread my resume and decided to hire me. Maybe he sneezed and got me approved. I'm just an angler and fin seller, you know. It's also possible that your Endfield system got too many loopholes, since a freezer can get treated as frontline combat hardware. Anyway, I got in. 
Okay. Since no one is shooing me away, I'll try to share my true knowledge. It's not going to be engineering or tactics. I'm talking about Angling. Don't underestimate Angling. It's outdoor meditation for true anglers. Those who don't know anything call it old boy's excuse to be lazy. I'll tell you about angling with the Endfield lingo. It is a miniaturization of a tactical operation. You got a bait, a hook, deception, and patience. So, who ends up slipping? Who gets hooked? Who becomes bait? And who enjoys deep fried fins on the shore? It's all about luck and vision. 
Now let's take a look at two basic terms — float angling and bottom angling. 
What is float angling? It's just scattering the bait in the water and looking at your float. You may think you caught something when the float moves a little. But when you lift your rod with excitement, you realize the fin never bit, and is in fact "laughing" and blowing bubbles at you. Some fins just take two bites and swim away. And some don't even like the bait. They just snag the line a bit and take you for a fool. It's like a turf battle. The bandit gives a funny look and you think he's about to make a move... But turns out he only remembered that he forgot about the spices for the fin stew. Angling is not about mysterious techniques. It's all about not snapping your rod after twelve missed pulls. 
So what is bottom angling? You dig a hole for yourself and then sink a bait. And then ... nothing else happens. The fins just ignore what you did. Maybe they'll roll their eyes before moving on. I used to know a gang advisor who is an expert in bottom angling. He always says: "Stop moving, son. They fear you more if you stay still." So, Senhor Advisor would spend all day on his second-hand rocking chair while they break our legs out there. And then he would squint his eyes and go: "Look. The enemy has taken the bait." — Take the friggin' bait. I hope the old bastard shits rocks and dies. I was the friggin' bait. 
Got a little carried away. Anyway, angling is a great sport. Just start angling if you wanna know how fun it is! In my humble opinion, it is far healthier than sitting here looking into the cold, dark space... So your question is, why am I even here? 
Decent canteen food and no one's clocking my naps. Pretty nice place, actually. 
 — Alesh's contribution to the Hobby-Sharing Get Together

War Song of the Samifjod
Sun melts the snow,
Under the frozen earth, shadows flee. 
But our wandering does not end. 
Sun splits the clouds, 
In the forest, rain departs. 
But our warfare does not stop. 
Lift shields, don plates, 
Fate holds us here. 
Under the sun, 
We bleed and fight.

After arriving on Talos-II from Terra, the Feranmut Sami ended His years-long drift and chose a plot of land within the polar circle, settling there along with the Myrkwood He carried on His back. Under the Feranmut's protection, the Sami people enjoyed a brief period of peace. But soon, with the destruction of the Cosmic Gate and the outbreak of the First Aggeloi War, the Feranmut Sami gave His life to protect the Sami people, falling in the North Pole. The Sami people barely had time to mourn before they had to join in the construction of the Oathkeepers' fortress. What followed was a long campaign that has continued to this very day.
When Typhoeus awoke on Rhodes Island and learned of her people's current mission, she immediately packed her bags and headed north. But after traveling a great distance to the Oathkeeper's fortress, a Sami Snowpriest just back from the battlefield gave her a pat on the back of the head, a slap reeking of earth, and turned her away at the door.
"Come back when you are taller than your bow, then you can go to war."
Though Typhoeus insisted that she was simply petite, no one believed her. After all, her hands had yet to develop the thick calluses that came from years of drawing a bow.
Lost and dejected, she could only board a wagon bound for Myrkwood to meet the kin she had never known. This was the Sami she remembered, the environment, the customs, the language, the accents, all preserved. Yet at the same time, it all felt foreign to her. In the settlement, there were only the elderly, the wounded, and the children. Those who could still bear arms had all chosen to head to the front lines, guarding that line forged of flesh and blood, holding back the Aggeloi's march southward.
Typhoeus, lost and adrift, remained in Myrkwood. She soon learned that after the fall of Sami, His legends had also been shattered. The elders who knew the old tales had turned to bone on the battlefield alongside Sami himself before they could pass the stories on. So Typhoeus, unable to fight on the front lines, decided to gather those legends and preserve them.

Endmin, did you know? The fall of Sami was Sami's own choice. The people accepted Him and followed without hesitation.
I found a Foldartal used for divination in Myrkwood. On it was recorded a "communication" between the Snowpriest and Sami.
Before He descended upon the north, He had warned the people of Myrkwood that He had long foreseen a cruel and protracted war. He would have to go north and, at some future moment, sacrifice Himself to protect all living things.
He gave His people the chance to leave...
But on the Foldartal were the people's response—
The will of Sami is the will of the Sami people. The mission of Sami is the mission of the Sami people. We will go north with you.
The hunt never ends.

After the Qingbo Stockade incident, we initially expected to receive a confused, grieving, or angry operator. In preparation, we had arranged some psychological intervention measures to help ease her trauma. Yet, when Tangtang arrived aboard the Dijiang via tele-protocol, her face was lit with a bright smile, not a shadow of distress in sight.
Supervisor Perlica reminded us that despite the complexity of her community, Tangtang managed to rally her scattered people with her own charisma. This proves she possesses a resilient spirit capable of bearing significant responsibility.
And indeed, Tangtang proved far more perceptive than we had imagined. Her awareness and sensitivity to situations are second to none. In planning the subsequent development of Qingbo Stockade, she consistently prioritized the welfare of its residents, skillfully ensuring that every individual, young, old, sick, or disabled, was accounted for with a blend of boldness and attentiveness, guaranteeing no one would be overlooked or forgotten amidst the busy tasks. This quality is particularly valuable to us: in work involving diverse cultural practices, having a guide who understands the complex local interpersonal dynamics and ecosystem saves us significant communication costs in our development efforts.
Tangtang has adapted to life aboard Dijiang remarkably quickly. At times, we see her walking alongside Chen Qianyu, the Endministrator, or Supervisor Perlica, her eyes sparkling, tail swaying gently. She's also made some new friends, giving them affectionate nicknames in the style of Qingbo Stockade. Moreover, everything about Dijiang seems to fascinate her, especially the canteen's vending machine... She circled it several times on her first day. An operator kindly stepped forward to show her how to insert coins and press the colored buttons to get a drink to roll out. She listened quietly, though it was hard to tell if she fully understood... That evening, the vending machine triggered an alarm, and Operator Xaihi ended up having to retrieve a stuck "Tangtang Cert" from the coin slot.
After several months of observation, our conclusion is that: not only does Tangtang not require psychological support from us, but her presence has, in fact, infused Dijiang with renewed vitality.
When we discussed this with operators familiar with her, Chen Qianyu remarked with a smile, "Though Tangtang grew up by the water, she's more like an unquenchable flame. A passing storm might dampen it, but that spark quickly reignites and burns bright again."
One afternoon, we overheard Tangtang chatting with someone, her tone as candid as ever: "The Chief's head isn't that big, kiddo. I can't keep trying to figure things out, you know. It'll just make me dumb!"

Tangtang is a member and primary representative of Qingbo Stockade. She joined Endfield Industries for personal reasons and is currently serving as Head of Endfield's Qingbo Stockade Liaison Office.

Operator Tangtang stands as perhaps the most distinctive individual among the diverse personnel the Endministrator has invited aboard Dijiang. Much like our first meeting... Apologies, I need to retrieve the recorded footage stored in my database:
"Thwack! Thwack!"
"Hey, what's this thing doing on a big airship? Looks like a three-headed iron tuskbeast. Kinda dumb if you ask me..."
"Operator Tangtang, I'm here for your onboarding inter— No, please don't slap my panel. I'm a personnel assistant from Endfield Industries..."
"So you're one of Darkmask's crew! You should've said so sooner, Old Iron-face! Here, I've got some good stuff I brought for my new Fam. Go crazy!"
After I repeatedly insisted I had no need for any Tangtang Certs, ores, or jewelry, Tangtang enthusiastically pulled a ring-shaped ornament made from natural materials from her pocket. I believe it could be defined as a woven bamboo floral wreath. She placed the wreath over one of my panels, then curiously began tapping the other two: "You're sharper than those Wuling tin toys! Why don't you come join me in Qingbo Stockade? Come on, call me Chief!"
My assessment of Tangtang aligns with others': cheerful, straightforward, unpretentious. She possesses a childlike heart, brimming with passion and curiosity toward everything... If I had to summarize her in a few words, I'd choose "a child in the midst of growing up." However, I absolutely cannot join Qingbo Stockade and conquer Talos-II with her... This has nothing to do with the endless stack of personnel files I have to process. It just doesn't quite align with Endfield's regulations.
To avoid injuring Tangtang's hands and to prevent myself from suffering "mechanical" concussion, I really should consider how to stay out of her way... Strangely enough, she always manages to find me.

DOCUMENT: HR recruitment log from the Shaynwood mail distribution station 
When that Cautus woman stepped through the door, I noticed that big red patch on her clothing. It looked about two or three days old, already starting to turn black. I asked if she needed any help, but she just said she wanted a job. She probably saw that hiring notice outside and got interested. 
"It's just ketchup," she said, "Nothing to worry about." 
"You sure are one helluva messy eater, young miss." I responded with an awkward smile. 
I'm not used to talking with pretty-looking people, and the town of Shaynwood did not give me much practice. The closest TGCC city is 368 klicks away, and the nearest frontier mail depot is about 110 klicks down the road. It was three in the afternoon. The most comely female usually frequenting my place would be the burdenbeast looking for grass outside the door. I assumed this Cautus had started her trip from the city 368 klicks away, with her next stop 110 klicks down the road. Her direction was interesting. Most people would travel in the opposite direction. 
Just last night, I heard about some Landbreaker-related altercation 23 klicks away. Armed battery involving six individuals. Five were injured and one escaped. The UWST Security Bureau operating in the frontiers messaged me to look out for individuals traveling alone. Might just be the fugitive. 
"The notice posted outside says you're looking for a mail courier," the Cautus said, pointing behind her with her thumb. 
"Ah, yeah. That's right. Your predecessor resigned just two months ago." 
"My predecessor? Are you saying that I'm already hired?" 
"Well, know how to drive? What type of vehicles? We don't care about licenses here. Count all the vehicles you know how to ride." 
"Six, including trucks, I think." 
"Awesome!" I said, "You nabbed the post. Start working tomorrow! I'll also need you to show me your ID and complete this form. Just for the records." 
I pushed her the form and a pen through the tiny window. She completed the form without much of a thought and pushed it back to me. She also gave me a big, glowing smile. What an understanding, kind, and cooperative lady! 
Then she started unloading her questions to me, as though she asked them a million times before. She also started arranging her accommodations as though she owns the place, "Can I park my car at the back? I'm talking about that overgrown plot behind the iron gate. Yes. Mmhmm? No problem. So, got any Originium power pylons here? I gotta fix my ride. It's down. And what's the network password? Got enough bandwidth on the thing? Yes. For movies. Wooo. Not bad... You don't say, you're inviting me ... to your place? Ooh. A dinner date? That's not what you meant? With your gramps, Postmaster Laine? Say, aren't you way too young for this, kiddo? Much appreciated, but I'll just sleep in my car. Don't worry. I'm used to it." 
She gave me a few winks before slowly swaggering her way through the door. 
I suddenly remembered that I had to check her form. Lo and behold! 
NAME: Secret, but yours for 60000 T-Creds. 
AGE: Forget it, kiddo 
ADDRESS: People will pay for this, you know 
RELATIONSHIPS: It's complicated 
EXPERIENCE: Professional traveler 
HEALTH INFORMATION: Essentially safe and hazard-free 
............
