DOCUMENT: Log of Captain Akekuri's interview regarding Operator Estella's background check 
Given the extraordinary circumstances of the operator in question, Captain Akekuri met me beforehand to discuss the operator's background and showed me a number of relevant physical and documentary information. 

EXHIBIT: A photograph 
An old photograph shows a little Feline girl with silvery-white hair, happily sitting on a wooden rocking chair. A young man and woman sit beside her, their hands resting on her shoulders. Together, they look like a happy family. 
Information from Akekuri revealed that this was a photograph taken 10 years ago in the study of Estella's family home. The place is now a ruin. The Aggeloi and the Blight forced them to move. The family brought their entire savings and traveled to La Fantoma with the aim of settling down in that city. 
However, the family did not achieve their goals. Captain Akekuri next displayed a newspaper cutting that recorded how Estella's family was swindled by an investment scheme and lost almost the entirety of their savings. 

EXHIBIT: Old newspaper cutting 
MacDoff Financial Scheme Breakthrough: Criminals Splurge and Decimate the Victims' Savings 
Reported on the 9th of this month (Correspondent: Meralda). Bernard MacDoff, the chief suspect behind the super-massive financial scheme that shook Talos-II with the sheer scale of fortunes involved, was finally apprehended just yesterday after years of hiding. 
In-depth investigations by our judicial system discovered that the criminal organization had devised a massive fraud scheme, luring unsuspecting investors with promises of generous returns. Principals from new investors were disguised as “payments” to older investors, creating the illusion that the scheme was generating massive profits. Many unsuspecting companies and individual investors were enticed to increase their investments in the MacDoff scheme. Such illegal financial operation of paying older investors with money from the new is a complete abomination of genuine investments that aim to generate true value. 
Persistent efforts by our law enforcement agencies paid off when MacDoff was finally brought to justice. He will be facing the full severity of the law. Unfortunately, the MacDoff gang has either splurged or transferred their illegal gains during their escape and hiding. After the case was filed, the amount of assets recovered and returned to the victims was a paltry sum compared to their losses. This means that despite arresting the chief suspect, the massive losses incurred by many companies and individual investors can no longer be salvaged. 
This case is a stern warning to the general public: Money doesn't fall from the skies. Investors are advised to remain vigilant and alert. Be wary of intricately designed investment traps created by various criminal organizations. 

When the MacDoff case was closed, Estella's family had already joined the UWST and worked at Shaft 39 in the Northern Mineral Field. However, luck did not smile on this family. Captain Akekuri showed us another newspaper cutting. 

EXHIBIT: Old newspaper cutting 
Accident in the Northern Mineral Field Worsened by Landbreaker Raid 
Reported on the 19th of this month (Correspondent: Riise). A massive mining accident has occurred at Shaft 39 with many miners trapped in the pits. Surface facilities were also subject to a sudden Landbreaker raid at almost the same time. Many crew mates and their family members have gone missing. 
According to Chief Mineral Field Monitor Lyube, Shaft 39 was about to conclude their operations in the evening of the 18th when the shaft entrance collapsed after a loud explosion. Only a few miners closer to the surface managed to escape to safety. Search and rescue (SAR) operations are ongoing, and all SAR work is expected to complete by the morning of the 20th. The number of casualties is still unknown. 
Our correspondent also successfully interviewed Mineral Field Surface Facility Office Monitor Povkova. According to her, in the evening of the 18th, a large Landbreaker band appeared about 5 minutes after the massive explosion in the shaft. The raiders then began to vandalize and raid various surface facilities and buildings. Armed personnel of the UWST were defeated by the Landbreakers within minutes. Surface facility office staff and family members in the residences then started to run for their lives. Exact casualty figures are still being determined. Many escapees are still missing and cannot be contacted. Ongoing investigations have yet to identify a direct link between the mining accident and the Landbreaker raid. 
The UWST Commandery is extremely concerned with this incident and has deployed multiple teams to conduct SAR operations in the northern mineral field. We will continue to bring you the latest updates from the site. 

According to Captain Akekuri, Mr. Kerr (Estella's father) was rescued, very much alive, from the shaft. However, Estella was separated from her mother during the Landbreaker attack. UWST SAR teams quickly rescued Mrs. Kerr, but Estella herself was captured by Landbreakers. They brought her with them to the wildlands and subjected her to involuntary labor. However, her talents were unexpectedly revealed during this cruel experience. 
Operations Team Z7 infiltrated a Landbreaker camp and Captain Akekuri encountered Estella during that time. The dirt-covered girl verbally conveyed the geographical layout and defense deployment and even drew a map of the entire place on the sand. Estella's intel allowed Op Z7 to capture the camp and rescue all civilians with minimal losses. 
Akekuri was impressed with Estella's intel gathering abilities and invited her to join Endfield. Having spent many years in the wildlands, Estella also strongly desired to have a safe residence and joined our organization without hesitation. Captain Akekuri also added that this episode of extreme hardship in Estella's life has made the operator extremely adverse to any work involving heavy labor. 

All logs above have been transferred to the Human Resources Division for reference.

Gilberta first met them with a white bedsheet draped over her head, as she played hide-and-seek with the hospital's children. 
As the door creaked open, she floated like a dandelion seed over giggling kids, then whooshed straight at the intruder for a tackle-hug. 
"Hehe, gotcha!" 
She yanked off the bedsheet triumphantly, only to freeze. Not a giggling child, but a stranger. A figure in a specialized mask, tilting their head in bemused silence. 
"Oh..." 
Gilberta recoiled, hands snapping back to her chest. A flustered smile flickered across her face just as recognition dawned, stealing all words of apology. 
"That outfit ... that mask ... no way..." 
Gilberta had imagined countless ways they might meet, but never like this. 
"You must be Gilberta, right? I'm ... well, I think you already know who I am." 
Their voice carried no thunderous command, yet it etches itself into memory like a half-remembered lullaby. 
Gilberta's face burned crimson, replaying her earlier blunder. She stepped back only to catch her heel on a hospital cot, sending her sprawling onto its edge. 
"I-I ... didn't expect you here..." 
"I heard some kids had been rescued and brought in, so I came to check on them. What were you doing just then...?" 
"Oh, uh — hide-and-seek. The kids were getting bored, so I figured we could play a game to cheer them up a bit." 
"Hide-and-seek... I see." 
They picked up Gilberta's bedsheet. 
"Well then, since you caught me, does that mean I'm 'it'?" 
"Huh? But you are..." 
"They scheduled me to give a speech. But honestly I'd rather play with you and the kids." 
"..." 
"What's wrong?" 
Noting Gilberta's silence, the figure touched their own cheek in quiet bewilderment. 
"You are nothing like the rumors," 
Gilberta smiled in relief. 
"Is that so..." 
Confusion deepened. Freshly cleared for independent movement yet still adrift in memory’s fog, they stood suspended between protocol and instinct. 
"Alrighty, let me explain the rules," 
Gilberta said with a grin on her face. 
Ah, so this was them. That half-remembered silhouette, the voice murmuring at fate's periphery. 
She was grateful for the Originium Woods left behind, more grateful still for this place, this moment.

"A group of merchants lived on the fourth planet visited by the Little Engineer. They gave every star a number, and locked the numbers in the safe..." 
"Many academicians lived in the sixth planet visited by the Little Engineer... The Little Engineer saw their incredibly thick spectacles, and immediately ran away." 
"The Little Engineer bid farewell to the Gargantuan Feranmut of Industry. He shouted into the mountain valley, 'Let's be friends! I'M LONELY!' But the mountains only responded with echoes of echoes of echoes..." 
"And in the end, the Little Engineer collapsed in the sand... And uh, oh yeah! With a swoosh he got back to his feet and shook off the sand. He waved at his friends, grew a pair of sparkling wings, and flew toward the stars!" 

"This story is probably written by an author from Ga ... just where my home used to be. Terran stories are interesting, as long as they're not history! Alright, my little rascals, that's it for today. For next time, we'll—" 
"Miss Yvonne..." 
"Awww. You look really down. What's wrong?" 
"The Little Engineer is so sad... He could not find his home anywhere! And he made no friends. He's so lonely..." 
"And why did he fly? Is it 'coz ... 'coz he got eaten up by the Aggeloi?! The grown-ups keep lying to me about this..." 
Yvonne blinked a few times, then fished out of her pocket the toy that was cobbled together with hardware parts. The little thing resembled Tata, and glinted in the sunlight like specks of diamond dust. 
"The Little Engineer just couldn't find fitting companions, but that doesn't mean he's lonely! Look at this! This is the first companion he built for himself. He also built other interesting teammates. One makes ice cream, the other creates fireworks... Everyone of them was a loyal friend! And then—" 

Yvonne followed the light and raised her head. Clouds slowly rolled across a uniform sheen of azure blue. She could imagine Dijiang cruising along its carefree orbit high above the skies. Yvonne then lowered her gaze and looked upon the children of Valley IV, their faces glowing with hope for more stories. The silhouette of the vessel, the sparkling wings of the Little Engineer, starlight of half-a-billion bells, and a world of splendor and harmony flowed across her retina. 
Yvonne felt free. The tempo of her storytelling became lighter and faster. 
"And in the end, it wasn't the darkness you imagined! The Little Engineer left because he made new friends, received an invitation from the brightest stars, and got a new place to stay! Now, dry your tears and I'll reward you with a bonus story about the Endministrator! Yeah... So what do you want to hear? The one where the Endmin smashed the sun, or the one where the Endmin transformed a single Originium crystal into a million soldiers?" 
"Smashed the sun ... and a million soldiers?! The Endmin is so awesome! Are these stories true?" 
"Hmm. Are the stories true...? Well, I guess I'll ask the hero in question right after this!"

DOCUMENT: List of Candidates for the Vanguard Scientist Award 
Author: Luo Shiqiao 

After integrating observations for the three dimensions of innovation, influence, and adaptability, I recommend Tianshi Pan Yuan as the recipient for this year's Vanguard Scientist award. His work so far accrued a total of twelve academic achievements and he has attained six sustainable development goals for HAS. Very few awardees from the last ten years have achievements on par with his. And Da Pan is not yet thirty. 
Although I am his mentor, I can guarantee that my evaluations are completely fair and balanced. When Pan Yuan knocked on my door and described his wish to be on my project team, my first reaction was to turn him down. The young man had left a relatively poor impression with me back then. He played ping-pong with explosives, on fire. He also got several veteran (and well respected) Tianshi to perform tap dance on a digital poster of Creative Maolaguo Cuisine Lovers. He built several high-speed battleships from scraps, and attacked our subterranean cryostorage facility with his fleet. The entire building reeked of rotten fins for a month... Yes. I suppose these are minor misdemeanors that come naturally to the youths. HAS encourages all kinds of scientific exploration, and even I ended up in the emergency medical bay a few times back in my younger days. 
Certain youths play pranks to get attention. Some of them do so to sate their immense curiosity about the world. Pan Yuan doesn't quite belong to either of these categories. He is ... too smart. I saw disinterested boredom in his eyes when he was caught doing these pranks. After becoming his mentor, I realized that he committed these actions because he could. To put it in other words, he wanted to prove that he was simply better than anyone else in HAS — even when it came to pulling off pranks on campus. 
Joy comes from challenges. Take away the challenge and you deprive any opportunities for joy — and a joyless academic pursuit will never get far. A sculptor who spends every moment chipping away at stone would only leave a handful of works behind. Pan Yuan has proved to be most obstinate. This stone must be properly polished to reveal its true beauty. But only another slab of stone harder than him could hope to bring down his pride and chip away at his edges. 
I told him, "There are several Tianshi who made significant achievements in the field of rift research. They would be better mentors than me..." 
But Pan Yuan replied, "But there is a great mountain within me that must be conquered first. Your projects and research focus are the only things that match my goals." 
At that moment, I saw confusion, pain, and maybe a subtle dash of cautious hope in his eyes. Maybe my judgment on his character was not entirely correct. Perhaps something changed him. As long as he is persistent, I have faith he will change for the better. 

And if you must have a reason for not giving him the award ... there is the matter of his rather impulsive temperament. And also because he was cooking in the lab and deliberately mislabeled a tub of puffed rice as "Reducing Agent". Maybe he didn't want others to steal his food, but this action completely wrecked my first prototype!

EXCERPT FROM A NEWSPAPER CUTTING 
Firstly, let us offer sincere wishes to Master Shatterus, reborn to us! Secondly, let us offer sincere wishes to the Law that has blessed and protected us! Finally, let us offer sincere wishes to our fellow faithfuls affected by the Domus Collapse! Perhaps some of you are still performing clean up work despite having pulled an all-nighter. But when you retire to your bed and rest, be aware that you must, in a punctual manner, pay your respects to our Lord afar. Our Lord shall forgive you for compensating yourselves after an intense episode of labor. 
Now back to the Domus Collapse. The cause of the incident has been identified: Redrawing of the Cathedralis Domus of Codes by Sister Séraphine. The redrawing has caused our Domus, itself based on the ancient and splendorous architecture of Laterano, to undergo unexpected resonance with our massive dataflows. Hence, the Great Monastery Network collapsed for 0.836 seconds. Even fellow Cabalists over two hundred kilometers away felt its tremors. Your faithful correspondent arrived at the site to see that Sister Séraphine had buried her head in a server cabinet and temporarily cut off from any contacts with the outside world. Abbess Vronta and three Cabal leaders later convened an emergency meeting to solve the incident. The verdict for the violator shall be officially announced in the next Session of Exceptions. 
Your faithful correspondent believes that there are two sides to every incident. Every massive scale solution offers a minute trail to the future. For example, this incident once again triggered a rather passionate debate if we should, in this generation, continue to provide labor, resources, and constant vigilance to maintain the Domus of Codes, itself a technological marvel. If you wish to share your opinions, please mail them to Box 302, Via Confessa Sancta, Great Monastery. Finally, the Lord is always within our hearts and minds. Good morning to you all! 
— Excerpt from Comments on Good Morning Shatterus, an internal periodical published by the Cabal of Tranquility for internal communications 

DOCUMENT: A letter (in the form of a secret order) delivered to the mailbox of Supervisor Perlica 
RECOMMENDER: Vronta "The Knower of Veritas", Abbas of the Monasterium, Cabal of Tranquility 
RECOMMENDER'S ADDRESS: No. 116, Via Ritualis Benevolens, Great Monastery 

To the Honorable Supervisor of Endfield Industries, Miss Perlica: 
I hereby recommend Sister Séraphine Xaihi as the liaison of our party in the Originium Information Technology project jointly pursued by Endfield Industries and us, the Cabal of Tranquility. As Xaihi's guardian in the Cabal, I have witnessed how she grew from a tender, young child who loved the libraries to a... Pardon me, but the Law demands us to be forthright and act with consistency. And thus I shall give you the answer: She has grown into a Frost of Wisdom. 
Truth be told, souls that have not gained the enlightenment of the Law will be easily lost in the vast amounts of knowledge stored within the Cabal. However, Xaihi has managed, in her own accord, to identify a path within the great vault of data. After years of tireless perusal and contemplation within our vault of tomes, we opened the door and saw her remade: Intellect did not lead her astray into arrogance, but instilled a sense of sorrow within her eyes. It was then when I realized that she had seen the future we are headed toward. Of course, this intellect has led to quite an incident on our side, one that is on par with her previous attempt of system optimization. 
Though I place no blame upon her, she seems to have sunken into such depths of guilt where self-salvation seems impossible. Hence, I humbly request to let Sister Xaihi continue her good works at Endfield Industries. The Cabal is rooted in our past and history, and hence we are not the perfect place for nurturing a future that is too delicate, tender, and far away. Sister Xaihi is better suited for your path. 
I have absolute faith that she is capable of fulfilling the duties demanded of an Originium Information Technology expert. Please contact me anytime should you need further details. 
Sincerely, 

Vronta, Cabal of Tranquility

Shortly after the Wuling Science Station incident, Tianshi Zhuang was entrusted with managing several temporary shelters. Under her command, a strong line of defense between the disaster site and the safe zone was quickly established. She also provided essential support to personnel deployment, disaster site remediation, and supply distribution. 
Her exceptional performance during the disaster impressed the HAS leadership. Despite many other qualified candidates, they insisted on entrusting her with the rebuilding of Wuling Science Station. 
Under such pressure, Tianshi Zhuang immersed herself completely in research on Xiranite. At times, she even caught herself wishing she were a machine that never needed rest. 
In a sense, she already was one. The lab's countdown clock for Blight rupture simulations governed her every move, each tick tightening her focus. When the crisis eased, tension gave way to activity as she buzzed between the lab and the Monitoring Center like a fully wound-up clockwork doll. 
It was a period when she sacrificed much ... and missed even more. 
Then one day, something unexpected shifted her perspective. She looked up from her work, perhaps just to stretch, and overheard a conversation. 
"I'm starving, I really want hot pot..." said a newly joined Tianshi, acne still dotting his youthful face. Another Tianshi responded indifferently, "Stop thinking about food. You're here to do research." 
The young Tianshi gulped his coffee, patted his cheeks, and muttered, "Right. This isn't home. I should keep my mind on the mission." 
Tianshi Zhuang herself recalled how she felt dizzy and stunned by this incident, as though struck by a fierce bolt of Tianshi Lei Fa (Thunder Arts). 
When the dizziness faded, she clearly realized what she had neglected — the piles of food tins, stale air, exhausted faces, some colleagues curled up in corners asleep, and another opposite her with a back crooked after spending long hours at the lab bench. Desperately she searched for something green, only to find the glow of her terminal screen. 
She rushed outside in search of living green, but the pear trees along the path were close to shedding their wilted flowers. The daily routine of work kept her so trapped that she never noticed them in full bloom. 
In a lapse of stupor she had a flash back. There was a time when everyone gathered around her as she drew straight lines and gentle curves to draft a city upon a sheet of paper. 
What did she say then? 
She said Wuling City would be a home for everyone. 
So why had she forgotten? 
She had no answer for that. 
But she knew one thing: Better late than never. 
That evening, every Tianshi in the Academy heard Tianshi Zhuang's call. She raced through every departmental buildings as though possessed, loudly calling out for everyone to leave the labs and admire the falling pear blossoms. Many were taken by surprise and did not know how to respond, so she went door to door and urged everyone to seize what remained of spring. And when even that failed, she threw open the windows and let the petals drift into the offices. 
When people later spoke of that day, some laughed and said Tianshi Zhuang had worked herself out of her mind. She would only smile and say that she had worked herself to clarity.

The Popper Tactic was first proposed by Operator Alesh. Its theoretical basis was based on poppers, a type of lures often used by hobby anglers. According to Alesh's extremely detailed yet unverifiable explanations, the popper is a fake, buoyant fin. Poppers are meant to dance, glimmer, wag their tails, annoy, and finally piss off the foul tempered big fins to the point that they burst out of the deep. Simply put, poppers do this: "Dun wanna move? Whatever. Watch me pollute your turf, play dead, and nab your stuff till you come out and beat me — And then you'll realize that I got a co-star on stage with me." 

What? I need to explain what happened recently? Oh, that was just a basic covert ops job. Convoy needed to get through Route 17 but that LBs love the place. The bandits seized cargo, kidnapped people, and even took over radio stations. Late Night Traffic Radio literally became a stinking cesspit of crude breakkae. 
I was about to go fix my rod, you know, when I got the mission notification. And when I read the words "basic covert operations", I suddenly got overwhelmed by work procrastination. Anyway, before I left for the job, I took a look at the map and mumbled: "Ugh. Let's try the popper." 
Of course, nobody knew what I was talking about. Convoy probably thought it was some new weapon and they agreed without thinking. The naivety is astonishing. I mumble something to myself, and people went along. 
Anyway, it was something really simple: 
We dumped two trucks by the road and dressed them up like they broke down, along with a few crates of "firearms". Eh, don't get too excited. The crates were filled with bricks. We even sprayed "Class I Hazard" on the crates to make it look real, you know. And then we played an "SOS recording" with a trembling voice. Shit is for real, man. More real than that empty rod in my previous angling run. 
And the first breaker mob came as expected. They paced around the setup like a beast lured in by fresh fins, and got all hungry and excited. Everyone of them wanted a piece of the "free takeaway". 
It wasn't even over. I tweaked the SOS radio louder and the second mob arrived. The first group of boys got really pissed. They went from "I wanna bite" to "You're not getting a bite". These blightheads didn't even bother to greet and went straight to all out war at each other. Just like wild, rabid cloudbeasts scrapping for a fin. 
So the crew hid behind the slopes and enjoyed the breaker show. We even commented on their fighting styles while snacking on dried fin roasts — Man, it was buggly as hell. I remembered hustling as a harbor punk when I was a kid, and I still fight better than these dudes. 
When the battle winded down, we swooped in like professional crime scene photo-takers. Take some pictures and clean up the entire place. The dead, the disabled, and the maybe dead or disabled. Anyway, the breaker war didn't leave many who could talk. 
So the entire convoy got through. Some trucker even told me: "Bro, that was some masterful covert ops." 
I said: "Thank you. My OG plan was to look at the skies all day. Didn't expect an entire school of fins to show up." 
The biggest take away from this was me verifying a principle — Everything is like angling. Make things up along the way and finprovise. Way better than making detailed plans, IMO.

I found out that "Chen Qianyu" is always the first name in the invite list for all sorts of celebrations, retirement parties, and daily hangouts at various Endfield regional offices as well as Dijiang. Everyone would punch in "Chen Qianyu" first when writing their invitation mail. This is not an alphabetical issue. Otherwise, Antal should be the first name on the list. 
Chen Qianyu is marked by her incredible vibes and abilities to liven up the atmosphere of an otherwise somber cabin. Once she steps into a place, it would take her less than five minutes to get the most introverted operators to start talking and the most restrained operators to start smiling. However, she usually does not have to use too much diplomacy to achieve these effects. In fact, Chen's direct and straightforward nature means that tact and technique are things she needs when communicating with other people. Chen actually relies on other properties when she livens up the atmosphere. Several operators attribute this to her warm, passionate smile. Others believe that it is her excessive over-reactions and her ability to inflate ordinary-looking incidents into exciting moments. Certain operators would emphasize Chen's seemingly endless reservoir of new ideas that bring about joy and happiness during recess, even for those unskilled in socializing — An example would be the tradition of office chair racing (which has been re-instated with Chen's insistence). Chen also actively took over Movies Aboard Dijiang, though most of her picks happen to be martial arts films from Yan. According to a few operators, when being a friend and listening to their accounts of the day, Chen could bring up points they had overlooked. Her inputs sorted out seemingly convoluted incidents as neatly as her meticulously combed and kept twin ponytails. 
During the retirement party of an elite operator, Supervisor Perlica got a little tipsy after going through a few glasses of Tunneling Nidwyrm bloodbrew (low kohlic content). While Andre snoozed on the sofa and Chen, surrounded by a crowd, trimmed the engineer's eyebrows with a pair of scissors, the Supervisor suddenly blurted out, "Chen has the power to make people feel safe." 
"What? It's so loud in here... Feel safe? I never heard these words from you before, Supervisor." 
Chen seems to regain her vigor by simply hanging around people. Even if her schedule were packed with field operations, she would do whatever she could to show up at various gatherings. She would liven up the event and then leave without a sound. When asked about this, Chen would say she was born without a serious need for sleep. 
"Wait. Operator Chen probably uses up more stamina and energy than most people, right? Sure, she might have training in esoteric Yanese techniques, but how can anyone maintain such levels of energy on just three hours of sleep per day?" 
"Speaking of which, I actually saw her dozing off during her meditative sessions..." 
Supervisor Perlica shook her head, "Chen is ... determined to shoulder the brunt for everyone. Once she has set her mind onto something, persuading her to give up is extremely difficult." 
"Oh? I thought Chen's a really easy-going person..." 
"Maybe she's just a little slow." 
"Supervisor Perlica, did you just say something bad about Chen?!"

"The Pack sent a tiny pup to talk? Did old Rozzan and his crew kick the bucket or something?"
Rossi glanced at Erik, who was roaring with laughter along with his crew, and instantly lost any interest she might have had in the leader famously known as the "Cannon of the Wildlands".
This was Rossi's first time handling the clan's ... "business". A week prior, a merchant convoy bound for the Luppino family had been intercepted by Erik. Out of respect for the Pack's name, they hadn't dared touch the couriers, but a sizable portion of the goods meant for return had gone missing. With Catello absent from the clan at the time, Rossi had volunteered, eager to prove her mettle with this particular "deal".
But at that moment, Rossi was starting to regret her decision. This trip was even less interesting than a hunting trip in home turf. The so-called "Cannon of the Wildlands" was wriggling his bulky, bloated body while slapping the table with his hand. From the moment she'd walked in, he'd done nothing but attempt to provoke her.
True strength is reserved, unyielding, never showing a crack. That was a lesson Rossi had learned within the clan. No one, not even Rozzan or the Elder Wolves, ever boasted so crudely about their violence.
"Nonno Rozzan told me this is 'business.' From where I stand, every deal has one side that profits, and another that takes the loss."
Rossi's eyes swept across the tent. The scent of gunpowder drifted to her nose, and she pinpointed where the other side had planted the explosives. The amount was small. Clearly, killing her wasn't the goal. A live wolf seemed far more useful to them.
"The Pack doesn't mind letting our business friends wet their muzzles a little. Unfortunately, I haven't passed my rite of passage yet, so I'm not a true member of the Pack. And I only want profit. I don't do losses."
"Looks like the Pack isn't planning to sit down and talk this out properly, eh?"
A flicker passed through Erik's eyes. The bandits around them grew serious, some already resting their hands on their weapons.
Two swordsmen, two axemen, and probably several casters lying in wait outside the tent. Judging by their positioning inside, it'd be tough to clear them out quickly. So—
Having assessed the situation, Rossi toyed with a fork on the table, waiting for the right moment.
"Listen. From the very first day I set foot in this blighted place, someone's been blabbering non-stop in my years. I can't do this. I can't kill that. I must follow the rules — the Code of the Pack."
Erik's agitation grew. He stared hard at the girl who'd come alone. All these preparations were meant for Rozzan of the Pack. But the old man sent a bratty girl instead... Erik felt insulted.
"The Code? It's written by those who are bigger and holds more power!"
Erik hefted his cannon. The Pack prized their kin. Taking this girl hostage could prove far more useful.
In a flash, a fork shot toward Erik. Rossi sprang from her seat and suddenly disappeared. Erik swatted the utensil away and raised his weapon to aim.
"Behave and be still."
A dagger pressed against the back of his neck.
The surrounding bandits finally drew their weapons, but it was too late. 
"STOP! DON'T GET ANY CLOSER!" Erik yelled, feeling a chilling prick of cold against the back of his neck.
"Counting on those casters at the door to bail you out? But that's odd ... it's way too quiet. Seems my clan wrapped things up even faster than I did. What were you saying again? Oh, right ... the Code..."
The icy tip of the blade seemed to press an inch closer.
"Do you understand what the Code of the Pack is?" Rossi sheathed her dagger.
Erik whirled around, furious. All his careful planning, ruined by a child like this? "I gave the goods to the Bonekrushers. Try and take them back if you have the guts for it! Once they've wiped you out, then I'll be writing up a new Code for this turf!"
"What did you say?"
A killing intent he had never felt before radiated from the girl standing before him.
Erik didn't know the price of bringing up the Bonekrushers around this girl, but he was about to learn. And soon.

Looking at the wrecked tent, Rossi couldn't help but sigh.
"Business is such a hassle."

Mr. Dolly's Game IV 
The day Ardelia boarded Dijiang with her sample box, she realized something was missing. 
"Where's Mr. Dolly...?" 
Invisible to most people, this fluffy creature was already happily wandering around Dijiang. 

In plain sight, Xaihi bowed apologetically to the empty space and said, "My sincere apologies, I did not mean to step on you, noble invisible being." 
"Something just barged in here!" "Who licked half the hotpot soup base!" The canteen buzzed with surprised shouts. 
"Who changed my alarm sound to 'baa baa baa'!? Oh no, oh no... I'm going to be so late for sword practice!" 
"It must be a ghost! And it's pink! Oooohhh, I'm calling dibs!" Yvonne dashed down the hallway excitedly. 
When Ardelia arrived, she found the Endministrator crouched by the door, slowly extending a hand, as if waiting for some silent consent. 
Mr. Dolly gazed at the Endministrator a moment before leaning in, letting the fingers sink into its thick wool, without a word. 

"That devout sister... pays little mind to anything beyond the pursuit of wisdom." 
"The cheerful chef? Oh, he hides weightier thoughts behind that grin. Don't mistake his ease for carelessness, not until his burdens are settled." 
"The girl who dreams of being a master pugilist... Will she wake from those dreams? Or will she bend the world to match them?" 
"And the one who shares my shade of pink... She's already found her path. Already happy." 
On the Bridge, Ardelia sat with Mr. Dolly beside her. Beyond the viewport, stars flickered like distant lanterns, and Dijiang itself slumbered in the quiet dark, a silent giant adrift in the cosmos. 
"As for the masked one..." 
Mr. Dolly flicked its ears and let out a soft, satisfied 'baa' — as if saying, "You can trust the Endministrator."

DOCUMENT: A funeral speech 
It was an ordinary morning, like all the other mornings that HAS had received before. But when the sunlight poured into the office, my husband had already passed away in his dreams. 
He committed his entire life to the Hongshan Academy of Sciences — Naturally there was a time when I hated it. Whenever I stepped into the corridors to deliver his meal, I felt only annoyance when I heard the all-knowing Tianshi debate each other. I didn't care if they were trying to get permanent tenure, jostling for higher positions, or really trying to get people fed. I didn't want to know why they were creating stacks of paper with no actual benefits to the environment. None of these mattered to me. 
I didn't understand why they would neglect their own lives just so others could survive and live theirs. It felt as though "survival" was a canon rule of the Academy, or an abstract concept. Perhaps their entire philosophy, career, and even existence was just part of this obsession of theirs. 
............ 
With my own hands I buried my daughter's dress at this public cemetery many years ago. She was one of the 113 who left us in the early days of the Wuling Science Station. 
...My husband and I had not talked for years. When I learned that my darling girl's vital signs ceased, he was carrying out the consecutive voting process with the old Tianshi. He only called me after three days. I was in tears when I asked why we couldn't bring the children's remains back home. He only told me it was impossible. At that time, the only wish on my mind was to strap myself with explosives and take my husband and those old academicians to the grave — that is ... until two incredibly young Tianshi opposed the vote. One was Viceroy Zhuang, and the other was an Ursus. The latter made quite a scene at HAS and soon left Hongshan after submitting his resignation. 
I thought the young lad, having expressed his disagreements in such a physical manner, wouldn't attend the funeral. But I saw him before everyone gathered here. He grew up and matured. He came quietly, and left just as quietly. He shared no words with anyone ... and left nothing but a jar of Mrs. Pepper. 
And now with my hands I buried my husband. I still detest HAS for having devoured my entire family. Yet I know that he ... that child, and every young Tianshi standing here with us whom my late husband had mentored, you have nothing but love for the Academy. 
At least he had flowers and his favorite hot sauce by his side when he left us. 

FILE: Repaired audio log 
"Dozens of hours had passed. Unfortunately, we have picked up no vital signs in the vicinity of the Very Large Rift. Since we have a unanimous consensus, we shall act upon the decision and cease all SAR operations." 
"Objection! I'm not going to argue whose proposal it was and how it ended up this way! But at least have the common decency to bring our people out, dead or alive! How could we even face their families after this?! Zhuang Fangyi, don't you dare side with them!" 
"Calm down and let me say something. Professor Huang... I believe Tianshi Pan is right. Giving up right now goes against the collective as well as individual spirit espoused by the HAS. I recommend continuing our SAR efforts." 
"Zhuang, I couldn't believe you actually agreed with Tianshi Pan on something, but this isn't the moment or place... Listen to us. This isn't giving up. We simply couldn't get it done. As Tianshi, you should use the balance of reason and understand this is us weighing the living against the dead. Now, get back to your seats." 
"Couldn't get it done?! Then think of something to get it done!" 
"Not everyone is like you, Pan Yuan..." 
"[Yanese expletive]."

"I really like Tianshi Zhuang, but I don't seem to know her well." Every operator who worked with her feels this way. 
Tianshi Zhuang's past is easy to trace. Any visitor to Wuling City can get the basics from a local tour guide or receptionist. For those who wish to know more, simply dig deeper into the archives of the Tianshi Bureau Academy to peruse her publications, though reading them all takes some dedication. And those who manage to do all that would have a clear picture of the Tianshi — A scientist deeply immersed in her work, a Viceroy who has dutifully served Wuling for a decade. 
If you wish to set aside Tianshi Zhuang's titles and know her personally, seek out an opportunity to be her coworker. Most people describe their first impression of her as the soothing gusts of Wuling City in March: gentle, comforting, and refreshing. As a coworker, Zhuang could unravel even the most recalcitrant of problems. She would be the cool midsummer breeze that takes away frustration and restores balance. The comfortable peace would last until your experiment hits a bottleneck. And then you'd sense a storm quietly brewing beneath her composed exterior. 
Her speech would change. It becomes quick and relentless, like a sudden downpour of which few can keep pace. Her stride would quicken. Every step a violent gust, sending reports flapping and fluttering off the tabletops. And finally, her problem-solving would transform. Like a blitz, she strikes directly at the source of the issue to completely shatter it, a guiding flash of light in the face of doom and gloom. 
Soon enough, the problem is no more. The storm subsides. 
You might think you know Tianshi Zhuang after several tumultuous rounds of collaboration. But as you catch your breath, you would realize that you only saw her scholarly side of Her Viceroyalty more clearly. And then it hits you: she never talks about herself. Not to you, not to anyone. 
You had stepped into the eye of the storm — and found nothing but stillness. 

DOCUMENT: Hongshan Evening News Vol. 8 
Obituary 
Surgeon Zhuang Hanqing, a distinguished scholar at Hongshan Academy of Sciences, passed away due to illness last Sunday at 6:23 AM at Hongshan First Hospital, aged 42. 
A family memorial and farewell service will be held this Thursday in the main hall of Hongshan Funeral Home.

Zhuang Changqing: Has anyone seen Fangyi? I've been busy all day. Just realized she's not in the mourning hall. 
Zhuang Daiqing: Don't worry. I'm with her now. 
Zhuang Changqing: That's a relief to hear... I'm glad you're here. She's just a child, and this is such a heavy loss.

<@profile.key>Letter from TGCC 
SENDER: Shiba Trading 
RECIPIENT: Human Resources Division at Endfield Industries 

Dear HR Team at Endfield Industries, 
Greetings. 
My name is Shiba Yoko, mother of Shiba Momiji. Pardon me for reaching out in this manner. 
As the CEO of Shiba Trading, I am accustomed to addressing matters with logic and efficiency. Yet as I write this letter, I find myself overwhelmed by emotions. 
Momiji is my only daughter. Her father met my younger brother while serving in the war against the Aggeloi. That bond eventually brought him into my life, and later, we had Momiji. While I was the strict teacher in her upbringing, her father and uncle were her playmates and protectors, filling her childhood with laughter and idealism. 
Everything changed after the Crusade against the Aggeloi ended ten years ago. Her uncle never returned, and her father came back a different man — only to leave home not long after. 
Since then, I have raised Momiji with care and intention, preparing her to carry forward both our family and our business. I shielded her from the very things that once tore our lives apart. She set aside her childhood game of "fighting Aggeloi" and turned her focus to her studies, growing into a diligent, outstanding young woman. She has never once let me down. 
And yet, upon graduation, she made an unexpected decision — joining Endfield Industries and volunteering for front-line duty. 
I was taken aback and deeply upset. We argued incessantly, and our relationship suffered. 
But over time, I came to realize this was not just a reckless impulse. The same sense of justice and idealism that once guided her father lives on in her. Though these ideals may have cost her a carefree childhood, they now give her purpose — and strength. 
I no longer oppose her decision. She is determined to prove her worth, even if it means risking everything. That is a resolve I cannot deny. 
I respectfully ask that you keep her safe, as much as circumstances allow. But please understand that my daughter is more than just academically gifted. 
Thank you for supporting her journey. 

 Shiba Yoko</>

<@profile.key>This was Adelheid's first culture shock. 
Seš'qa, the Stop, the capital of Witchcraft, the Sarkazian hub, the gathering spot of vagabonds... It was a city of names and she heard plenty of them. However, it was not until she alighted from the dirigible and stepping onto Seš'qa proper when she realized that "flight" was the most insignificant feature of this strange realm. 
The entire place seemed to be a never-ending stream of carnivals. Riot was engraved into the air itself. The decorative furnace that adorned the central plaza spewed waves of heat, clamor, and tons of laughter. Every street was lined with strange shops and signs. People rubbed shoulders in the crowd, chewing food with names that defy even the most dexterous tongues as they marched for the formation of giant figures looming in the distance — Rumors speak of a fighting arena as well as a fairground featuring Sarkazian culture, meticulously prepared for tourists when Seš'qa made itself available to them. However, the purpose of this administrative divisions seems rather limited when Seš'qa itself was already like a giant theme park. 
Adelheid's stomach started rumbling again. 
Perhaps it wasn't a good idea to accept that wandering peddler's invitation. She heard about Witching Hour, but she could never afford anything from this manufacturer. She only needed a broom to chase away the beasts back home. Like Seš'qa itself, the concept of proper weapons felt foreign and distant. "But I only flipped a truck toppled by the Aggeloi so it got back on its wheels. Why would anyone recommend me a job opportunity for that?" Adelheid started to wonder. What could she possibly do at this place? 
The peddler was far away, handling some registration procedure, stringing syllables and words that she could not understand. She suddenly realized that she knew nothing about the Sarkaz, despite being one herself. And is that powerful mercenary a Goliath? A man wore pendants dangling from his sharp ears. Did they mean anything? Everything was new. The peddler explained that her constant sense of hunger was a racial trait as well. But knowing this did not solve the problem. According to Sarkazian standards, her stubborn refusal to "feed" probably made her the one least qualified to talk about the rebellious nature of this city. 
Her stomach rumbled louder. Every time she felt afraid or helpless, impulse would find its way in and make it harder to control herself. And this was worse than usual. If someone asks, how should she answer? It would be inappopriate to say: "I'm sorry. I just don't feel like being a Nachzehrer."
There was still a chance to escape. The peddler's route would pass through a few more towns and villages. She could always apologize later. It would be best to find a place to hide and wait for the constant sideway glances to ease off... 
"What's happening to you?" 
The voice jolted her back from her increasingly sticky sense of anxiety. The lad tilted his head, his gaze more curious than confused: "There's free bread over there. Just tell the guard before you grab one. And there's also a pamphlet with a list of jobs. That's free, too." 
"I ... I'm sorry, I'm actually alright," she tried to get her breathing under control and ease the trembling out of her voice, "I'm just waiting for someone." 
"Oh. Okay, " the lad sniveled, "But you don't have to worry. Plenty of opportunities here. You'll find something to do. It took me two whole weeks as well." 
The lad was mature for his age and did not seem to believe in her words. Adelheid thought about it but chose not to argue. His expressions seem to exude strange powers that alleviated her worries. 
He gave her a pat on the shoulders before blending into a nearby crowd once more. She turned to look. It did not appear like a tourist attraction. Sweaty laborers worked on the scaffold as merchants frowned and wrote out their orders. A few well-dressed individuals flanked by mercenaries walked out of what seemed to be a fancy bistro. Everyone looked busy, yet all of them gave off the same relaxing vibe of that young lad. There were plenty of opportunities and she would figure something out. 
She saw the lad running towards the mercenaries, shouting angrily as he bundled their weapons. He was like a shepherd trying to herd a flock of giant, half-drunken beasts from their masters into the inn. The lad's tail was short and sharp, reminding her of her foster parents. 
The girl suddenly remembered the peddler saying something on the dirigible: "We got it to fly because the Sarkaz everywhere were facing difficulties. But when it started flying, we realized that plenty of others are facing hard times, not just the Sarkaz." 
Before it became a flying city of amusements, Seš'qa was a frontier outpost. Despite being involved with countless legends and serving numerous functions, it was a young outpost facing the unknown in the frontiers where humanity strove to build a new home. Life will always find a way. The outpost does not need to house everyone. It just needs to be "a stop", and that would be enough. 
And thus, after more than ten minutes of shock and awe, Adelheid began diverting her attention to the streets. Her eyes rested upon a massive pile of roasted stockbeast fillet glistening with grease. 
It was salty, so salty that it sent her heart racing wildly.</>

<@profile.key>DOCUMENT: Log of Captain Akekuri's interview regarding Operator Estella's background check 
Given the extraordinary circumstances of the operator in question, Captain Akekuri met me beforehand to discuss the operator's background and showed me a number of relevant physical and documentary information. 

EXHIBIT: A photograph 
An old photograph shows a little Feline girl with silvery-white hair, happily sitting on a wooden rocking chair. A young man and woman sit beside her, their hands resting on her shoulders. Together, they look like a happy family. 
Information from Akekuri revealed that this was a photograph taken 10 years ago in the study of Estella's family home. The place is now a ruin. The Aggeloi and the Blight forced them to move. The family brought their entire savings and traveled to La Fantoma with the aim of settling down in that city. 
However, the family did not achieve their goals. Captain Akekuri next displayed a newspaper cutting that recorded how Estella's family was swindled by an investment scheme and lost almost the entirety of their savings. 

EXHIBIT: Old newspaper cutting 
MacDoff Financial Scheme Breakthrough: Criminals Splurge and Decimate the Victims' Savings 
Reported on the 9th of this month (Correspondent: Meralda). Bernard MacDoff, the chief suspect behind the super-massive financial scheme that shook Talos-II with the sheer scale of fortunes involved, was finally apprehended just yesterday after years of hiding. 
In-depth investigations by our judicial system discovered that the criminal organization had devised a massive fraud scheme, luring unsuspecting investors with promises of generous returns. Principals from new investors were disguised as “payments” to older investors, creating the illusion that the scheme was generating massive profits. Many unsuspecting companies and individual investors were enticed to increase their investments in the MacDoff scheme. Such illegal financial operation of paying older investors with money from the new is a complete abomination of genuine investments that aim to generate true value. 
Persistent efforts by our law enforcement agencies paid off when MacDoff was finally brought to justice. He will be facing the full severity of the law. Unfortunately, the MacDoff gang has either splurged or transferred their illegal gains during their escape and hiding. After the case was filed, the amount of assets recovered and returned to the victims was a paltry sum compared to their losses. This means that despite arresting the chief suspect, the massive losses incurred by many companies and individual investors can no longer be salvaged. 
This case is a stern warning to the general public: Money doesn't fall from the skies. Investors are advised to remain vigilant and alert. Be wary of intricately designed investment traps created by various criminal organizations. 

When the MacDoff case was closed, Estella's family had already joined the UWST and worked at Shaft 39 in the Northern Mineral Field. However, luck did not smile on this family. Captain Akekuri showed us another newspaper cutting. 

EXHIBIT: Old newspaper cutting 
Accident in the Northern Mineral Field Worsened by Landbreaker Raid 
Reported on the 19th of this month (Correspondent: Riise). A massive mining accident has occurred at Shaft 39 with many miners trapped in the pits. Surface facilities were also subject to a sudden Landbreaker raid at almost the same time. Many crew mates and their family members have gone missing. 
According to Chief Mineral Field Monitor Lyube, Shaft 39 was about to conclude their operations in the evening of the 18th when the shaft entrance collapsed after a loud explosion. Only a few miners closer to the surface managed to escape to safety. Search and rescue (SAR) operations are ongoing, and all SAR work is expected to complete by the morning of the 20th. The number of casualties is still unknown.

<@profile.key>Shortly after the Wuling Science Station incident, Tianshi Zhuang was entrusted with managing several temporary shelters. Under her command, a strong line of defense between the disaster site and the safe zone was quickly established. She also provided essential support to personnel deployment, disaster site remediation, and supply distribution. 
Her exceptional performance during the disaster impressed the HAS leadership. Despite many other qualified candidates, they insisted on entrusting her with the rebuilding of Wuling Science Station. 
Under such pressure, Tianshi Zhuang immersed herself completely in research on Xiranite. At times, she even caught herself wishing she were a machine that never needed rest. 
In a sense, she already was one. The lab's countdown clock for Blight rupture simulations governed her every move, each tick tightening her focus. When the crisis eased, tension gave way to activity as she buzzed between the lab and the Monitoring Center like a fully wound-up clockwork doll. 
It was a period when she sacrificed much ... and missed even more. 
Then one day, something unexpected shifted her perspective. She looked up from her work, perhaps just to stretch, and overheard a conversation. 
"I'm starving, I really want hot pot..." said a newly joined Tianshi, acne still dotting his youthful face. Another Tianshi responded indifferently, "Stop thinking about food. You're here to do research." 
The young Tianshi gulped his coffee, patted his cheeks, and muttered, "Right. This isn't home. I should keep my mind on the mission." 
Tianshi Zhuang herself recalled how she felt dizzy and stunned by this incident, as though struck by a fierce bolt of Tianshi Lei Fa (Thunder Arts). 
When the dizziness faded, she clearly realized what she had neglected — the piles of food tins, stale air, exhausted faces, some colleagues curled up in corners asleep, and another opposite her with a back crooked after spending long hours at the lab bench. Desperately she searched for something green, only to find the glow of her terminal screen. 
She rushed outside in search of living green, but the pear trees along the path were close to shedding their wilted flowers. The daily routine of work kept her so trapped that she never noticed them in full bloom. 
In a lapse of stupor she had a flash back. There was a time when everyone gathered around her as she drew straight lines and gentle curves to draft a city upon a sheet of paper. 
What did she say then? 
She said Wuling City would be a home for everyone. 
So why had she forgotten? 
She had no answer for that. 
But she knew one thing: Better late than never. 
That evening, every Tianshi in the Academy heard Tianshi Zhuang's call. She raced through every departmental buildings as though possessed, loudly calling out for everyone to leave the labs and admire the falling pear blossoms. Many were taken by surprise and did not know how to respond, so she went door to door and urged everyone to seize what remained of spring. And when even that failed, she threw open the windows and let the petals drift into the offices. 
When people later spoke of that day, some laughed and said Tianshi Zhuang had worked herself out of her mind. She would only smile and say that she had worked herself to clarity.</>

<@profile.key>Mr. Dolly's Game I 
Shortly after joining Endfield, Ardelia visited a Blight-ravaged sector of Talos-II. The geological disaster had shredded a once-peaceful settlement, leaving fissures that pulsed with residual energy. Survivors bore wounds beyond the physical, their eyes hollow with the kind of trauma only disaster refugees know. 
Ardelia stayed at the shelter for a while. The wounded crowded steel cots — limbs lost, eyes vacant, voices severed by trauma. White curtains divided their suffering as medical monitors pulsed like weary hearts. 
Ardelia worked tirelessly — organizing supplies, changing bandages, murmuring "I understand your sorrow" to the wounded. Until a voice, serrated with grief, cut through: "You don't understand." 
It was a young girl. Small but fierce, she forced the words through gritted teeth: "You stand straight. Your steps don't falter. No disaster has carved its marks into you." 
The girl turned away, her voice fraying at the edges. "Stop. Just stop pretending. Maybe you've been sick, but you healed. That's luck we'll never taste. Our stories end in the same sentence: lifelong pain. So when you say you 'understand'... is that pity's cheap coin? Spare us." 
Ardelia stood there in her research coat, ponytail precise, steps steady, and eyes bright. The Originium had scoured the reconvener's illness away, attuning her to wind whispers and microscopic fractures in stone. Yet here, before those still drowning in pain, her engineered perfection rendered her mute. 
When darkness fell upon the land, Mr. Dolly appeared. 
It trotted between beds and corridors, leaving chaos in its wake — toppling medicine cabinets, upending tea trays, kicking a freshly filled hot-water bottle beneath pillows. Nurses cursed the sudden swelter; children shrieked about 'something furry' burrowing under their blankets. 
Ardelia chased Mr. Dolly into an old break room where she tugged at a canvas sheet to reveal a dust-choked piano. It stomped the keys, a discordant chime that jolted Ardelia into clarity. 
Ardelia approached, brushing away the dust. The yellowed keys stared back, a few bass notes dissonant but functional. She sat, fingertips tracing a tentative sequence of Leithanian arpeggios into the stale air. 
First piece ... second ... and as the third began, soft footsteps whispered from the hallway's depths. 
Mr. Dolly lay curled nearby, a silent cushion of warmth. The children nestled against its fur, their breaths syncing with Ardelia's piano as the notes wove through the stale air. 
The young girl came in as well, perching quietly in the farthest corner. 
"It still hurts," she murmured, "but when you play... the world becomes something worth enduring." </>

<@profile.key>Lemme introduce an old friend of mine. Wait... Yeah. I think we're old friends. Anyway, the story begins with my least favorite angling style — Drop-n-Yank. 
Drop-n-Yank is just like what it says. No lures, no baits, and no waiting for the fins to bite. Drop the hook, yank with all your might, and hope it stabs into something that you can plop in the bucket. They call it angling, but it feels more like violent muggery to me — Absolutely zero patience or technique. One hundred percent deadly. 
I saw the technique for the first time at an abandoned wharf. An old angler with scars all over his face dropped, yanked, and man, it was aquatic murder. Blood everywhere and the poor fin was still flapping. A bunch of kids and I learned how to drop-n-yank by hiding behind the barrels while chewing on tortillas. 
That was how I "met" my old friend. It was my first time doing the drop-n-yank and I pulled the thing up from the water. But it fought back and tore itself free. I couldn't forget that bloody wound and the disfigured eye. Ugh. I can still feel that eye staring at me. Of course, I didn't bother with human-fin relations back then. People have to angle when they get hungry, and we can't help it when things get ugly. 
When I was a punk kid, we lived like fins stuffed in a can. First thing we do in the morning was a headcount to see who survived and who got "devoured" by the streets. Stealing, mugging, and lying? Those were the survival techniques. We negotiated with fists. When you have to drop-n-yank for fins, you know how rough it was back in those days. 
Then some guy showed up. One that didn't treat us like feral wildlings. He taught us how to negotiate properly, how to step back a little, and how to protect those around us. He even handed me La Estrada. Told me that someone has to do something different for the city. I believed him, you know. Maybe I can clean up the biz and make a name for myself. 
Nights got real quiet in those days. I would sometimes angle for fins at the wharf. That was when I saw it again. It became a great fin. The monstrous thing always fought back, always broke free, and always swam its victory circle. It was laughing at me with that ring of ripples. 
So I fought with people in the day and the fin at night. And it lasted till ... my two most trusted friends gave me "Game of Gangs the Reality Show" plus a ton of backstabbing. They were like two insane raptorfins trying to off each other, and I paid an eye to get them to stop. On the day when the gang broke up, I sat at the wharf to see the waves breaking against the wall. We painted graffiti together as kids. Now there was nothing but froth. Our friendship became a dead fin. Scaled and scraped clean. 
That was also the day when I realized it had become an old geezerfin — Old dude also lost a lot of weight and its scales were falling off. The injured eye had already turned entirely white. It leaped out of the water and stared at me coldly. It was laughing at me and telling me how I deserved everything. I thought it was our last meeting. 
But just two days ago, I ran into the geezerfin during night angling after I closed shop — It was full moon and I knew old geezerfin bit the hook. Man, I know that deadly strength anywhere. The battle felt like it lasted a hundred years. You should have seen the splashes. Feels like Maymay testing out her explosives underwater. But I was the victor of the struggle. The line did not snap and I hoisted geezerfin out of the water. It looked way bigger than it did during its prime. I was about to lower it in the fin crate when I saw that — there was nothing on the hook. Even the bait was still intact. 
Did I actually hook the thing? Did it just come and leave? Or was it just my unresolved angst and dilemmas that used the cover of night to show themselves? I finally understood when the last ripples disappeared. "It" was no longer a simple fin. 
It had become my lingering disappointments and obsession, an embodiment of "what ifs" left behind whenever I see someone leaving or dying early. I even toyed with the idea using the Originium Arts to "hook" it out in its entirety — I knew its form, its wounds, its actions, and even the way it stares at people. It's living with me, and it's way more alive than it had been in water.</>

<@profile.key>DOCUMENT: Yvonne's work diary 
Day 3 after starting at that particular data section of the Æther rift. I can't see anything inside. All monitoring modules were knocked out. IR, EM, resonance responses — we got flatlined for everything. Not a single blip showed up. Sheesh. 
I tried to "read" the changes of that particular area with a smart sign language interpreter! And all I got was a bunch of errors and a single line that reads: "Failed to interpret data." 
We didn't just fail to monitor the stuff. The Æther rubbed it in our faces. We're completely blind to it. The only thing I'm certain of is this: It exists, and it's not very nice. 
I HATE THINGS I CAN'T SEE! 
............ 
Maybe I can change my approach. What would happen if I actively send data into it? Instead of just passively waiting for a response to come out of the output port, we should seize the initiative and interact with it instead. 
I tried three signal packs with different frequencies: (1) a standard greetings protocol; (2) a set of greetings I wrote myself in pulse-based format; (3) a set of static noise (the first note from the Movement: Genesis of the Universe, the Ætherside might like it). 
The results are just as predicted ... no responses. Fine. Be optimistic. Perhaps there was a response but receiving a radio wave transmission and emitting a response might take a while. If a single vibration takes at least 10 million years, then I have no choice but to keep Frost-e-Bytee on the receiving line. 
Perhaps I can try optical wave signals with various color codes. If that thing can see things, perhaps it'll like glittering stuff, like me! 
Plus light travels faster than sound! 
............ 
How many times did I fail again? Can't remember. Signal modulation, model simulations, and feedback monitoring ... none of it worked. The noise I'm getting sounds like the Æther laughing at me — I really hope it was laughing at me, because that means I'll unleash Frost-e-Bytee and ram some icy cold down its throat! 
I always believed that persistence will eventually identify a crack. But now I am beginning to wonder if this is a futile effort of exploration with no way out. 
We can't even "observe" this thing. How are we supposed to "decipher" it? 
The models I proposed and the devices I designed felt like childish gimmicks when compared to the Blight... 
............ 
Maybe the only thing I can do right now is to spin around on my swivel chair. Perhaps I gotta wait 10 million years for a miracle to happen. 
I might as well change my scientific approach. Time to build an invincible space armada. Let the ancient songs echo as I raise countless ... cities into the skies! Unfeasible? Maybe. But what can be more unfeasible than deciphering the Æther? 
I looked at those images of the Æther rift. I gazed at them long and hard. It devoured both sound and light. Even I got trapped within it — it crushed me and smothered me with eternal darkness. There is no escape for me. 
So why am I doing all this? To protect Talos-II...? To prove myself...? Because I got a grudge against Pa and Ma...? No. I think it all started on that day. I read about the Æther rift in the books and found it beautiful. So I snuck off to the Protection Band so I could observe it, like the giddy girl I was. The rift gave off a bright halo. Looking at it feels like staring straight into the sun. The piercing pain then gave way to a sense of indescribable horror and then it ... melted. 
It was a terror that got me bawling and trembling under my blankets late that night. My eyes swelled like peaches in the following morning — I looked gross. And I don't ever want to look like that again. So that's it: I'm going to decipher it. It's as simple as that. 
And I believe I can do it at Endfield. 
So once again, I punched the [SEND] button. A resounding KABLAM of epic proportions and ZERO hesitation. Gone and dusted. The darkness will be no more, and I shall return to daytime. </>

<@profile.key>DOCUMENT: A private letter 
Lamp: 
Where are you, darling babe? Your great granny, grand aunt, aunt, and sister heard (from me) that you quit your job and left home. They've got a ton of questions, and they are relentless. Even the best-fabricated story would breach under their endless drilling. Anyway, the family exploded when they learned you really left home, just as we expected. Looking on the bright side, I kept it a secret for 3 weeks. But Mama's gotta know where you've been all this time. 
I know our argument at Arlirye left quite a bad taste in the mouth. Mama still doesn't support your choice but when I got back home and sat down, I suddenly remembered that trip I had planned when I was a young gal like you. My bag was already packed and leaning right against the wall. I was that close to picking it up and marching through the door to get somewhere far away when I heard you. You were in your baby feeding chair and smiling at me with a baby knife and fork in your hands. And I stayed. I'm sharing this story with you because I wish to tell you that your hope of leaving home might be an inherited habit. 
Though your great granny likes to talk about it, the scenes that our pioneering ancestors witnessed after crossing the Cosmic Gate had already faded away into patches of mold on the wall. They were part of the gigantic convoy column, a great wall of vehicles that stretched all the way to the edge of the horizon. The truckers kept driving, up till the very eve of Severance. That was how we found our first pot of gold, the starting capital upon which we built our logistics business in Alloycarrot. However, as we spent longer and longer time chasing after mineral veins, our kin no longer felt at home when placed behind the wheel. 
Watch out for enemies on the road. Your TGCC job wasn't exactly low profile and we had a share of visitors. Rest assured, no one's going to hurt my darling baby doll. 
I'll handle the rest of our family for you. Don't forget to send us pictures from your traveling. 

Mama 

DOCUMENT: A private letter 
Mama: 
Finding network connection in the wildlands is no easy task. But a solo journey is everything I dreamed of. Sweet and beautiful. 
I stopped by New Wrankwood right after leaving home. They tried to recreate the scene to heal trauma, but it ended up quite disappointing, since no one was interested in the horror genre. And the place just wouldn't stop raining. I didn't like it. 
The Northern Corridor is my next destination, and I'll soon be reaching the edge of the Band. Just yesterday, a painter at the motel told me about the breathtaking natural landscapes waiting for me once I leave the Band cities. I intend to explore the old frontiers of the north. People say there are ruins that date back before the collapse of the Cosmic Gate. They're the things that great granny kept talking about, right? Don't worry about me getting into dangerous situations. I've been traveling with a group of Hannabit Circuit Songseekers. Once I find decent connection, I'll send you photos of me riding a burdenbeast. 
FYI, someone just piqued my interest. Whenever I found a place to rest my legs and talk to the locals, I would hear a name called the "Endministrator". Coincidentally, my itinerary basically matched this "Endministrator's" northward expedition. Is it possible that I've found my match in Talos-II in the field of professional traveling? 

Lamp </>

<@profile.key>DOCUMENT: HR recruitment log from the Shaynwood mail distribution station 
When that Cautus woman stepped through the door, I noticed that big red patch on her clothing. It looked about two or three days old, already starting to turn black. I asked if she needed any help, but she just said she wanted a job. She probably saw that hiring notice outside and got interested. 
"It's just ketchup," she said, "Nothing to worry about." 
"You sure are one helluva messy eater, young miss." I responded with an awkward smile. 
I'm not used to talking with pretty-looking people, and the town of Shaynwood did not give me much practice. The closest TGCC city is 368 klicks away, and the nearest frontier mail depot is about 110 klicks down the road. It was three in the afternoon. The most comely female usually frequenting my place would be the burdenbeast looking for grass outside the door. I assumed this Cautus had started her trip from the city 368 klicks away, with her next stop 110 klicks down the road. Her direction was interesting. Most people would travel in the opposite direction. 
Just last night, I heard about some Landbreaker-related altercation 23 klicks away. Armed battery involving six individuals. Five were injured and one escaped. The UWST Security Bureau operating in the frontiers messaged me to look out for individuals traveling alone. Might just be the fugitive. 
"The notice posted outside says you're looking for a mail courier," the Cautus said, pointing behind her with her thumb. 
"Ah, yeah. That's right. Your predecessor resigned just two months ago." 
"My predecessor? Are you saying that I'm already hired?" 
"Well, know how to drive? What type of vehicles? We don't care about licenses here. Count all the vehicles you know how to ride." 
"Six, including trucks, I think." 
"Awesome!" I said, "You nabbed the post. Start working tomorrow! I'll also need you to show me your ID and complete this form. Just for the records." 
I pushed her the form and a pen through the tiny window. She completed the form without much of a thought and pushed it back to me. She also gave me a big, glowing smile. What an understanding, kind, and cooperative lady! 
Then she started unloading her questions to me, as though she asked them a million times before. She also started arranging her accommodations as though she owns the place, "Can I park my car at the back? I'm talking about that overgrown plot behind the iron gate. Yes. Mmhmm? No problem. So, got any Originium power pylons here? I gotta fix my ride. It's down. And what's the network password? Got enough bandwidth on the thing? Yes. For movies. Wooo. Not bad... You don't say, you're inviting me ... to your place? Ooh. A dinner date? That's not what you meant? With your gramps, Postmaster Laine? Say, aren't you way too young for this, kiddo? Much appreciated, but I'll just sleep in my car. Don't worry. I'm used to it." 
She gave me a few winks before slowly swaggering her way through the door. 
I suddenly remembered that I had to check her form. Lo and behold! 
NAME: Secret, but yours for 60000 T-Creds. 
AGE: Forget it, kiddo 
ADDRESS: People will pay for this, you know 
RELATIONSHIPS: It's complicated 
EXPERIENCE: Professional traveler 
HEALTH INFORMATION: Essentially safe and hazard-free 
............</>

<@profile.key>"Why?"
The legendary senior business consultant of Seš'qa, one of the lead brand managers of the Witching Hour, the downtrodden Sarkaz merchant, "Bridge Builder" Fleming, was taken aback by this simple question. Though it came right out of the blue, Fleming quickly regained his cool, tidied his tie, and started counting the stars as he readied himself for the banter. 
The Feline who stood before him always made him tingle with a strange nervousness, ever since that snowy night. 
"Ahem. First thing first... We genuinely appreciate Endfield's acceptance of Adelheid. Seš'qa hereby extends its most sincere gratitude." 
"Good. That means you'll pay extra for her additional catering fees. Right?" 
"Trust me. Sending her to Endfield is considered a loss for our business." 
"Oh. You have a slogan for Last Rite ... the Princess of the War Court? Very loud and attention grabbing. Must have made you a fortune." 
Fleming laughed. He usually laughs as a means of dealing with his opponent on the negotiating table. But at this moment, he was laughing to give himself a chance to breathe. 
M3 paid no attention to Fleming's peculiarities. Her gaze was reserved for Adelheid, seated uncomfortably outside the office — Last Rite herself. Fleming sensed M3's curiosity. He cannot afford to miss the opportunity to regain his initiative. 
"What do you think of Miss Last Rite?" 
"I think she's hungry," M3 said without averting her gaze from the girl in question. Fleming tried to remember things. Rumors speak of the Feline's ties with the origins of Kazdel, and she hardly paid this much attention to other talents he recommended. "How could you let such a lovely girl starve?" 
"I swear..." 
"I think you need to pay an additional catering fee to Endfield Industries. Maybe we should set this sum to..." 
"I *SWEAR* this is for the best!" 
Fleming immediately realized that he had slipped. His opponent was simply trying to muddy the waters... No. She was just having a friendly banter. Why did he suddenly break his composure? 
"And why is that?" 
"Ugh... You know, a Nachzehrer in a cemetery with an extreme 'shame of consuming'... She has consistently refused to touch the deaths of others. Her constant hunger is only a natural consequence." 
"No, no, no... You got it all wrong..." 
M3 maintained her coy, relaxed tone. But that was not the worst for Fleming. What stressed him out more was the fact that she had not smiled ever since he stepped aboard Dijiang. 
"You know the Sarkaz. No amount of roasted steak fillets could fill an empty soul." 
"Soul? You believe in souls?" 
"Ahem... Every Sarkaz who benefited from the protection of the myriad souls believes in them." 
"I'm sure the myriad souls will be happy to know that," M3 finally moved her gaze away from the girl. She hesitated, a rare opportunity. But Fleming did not treat this as a good sign, "But the time does not match." 
"I understand... It took place over a century ago. Nevertheless, Adelheid is definitely a young girl of only seventeen or eighteen years." 
"Right. So, why?" 
Fleming kept his bitter smile inside. Nevertheless, he decided to confront this question directly. 
"I don't know. But like you said ... she remains very hungry." 
"Even with 'that thing' following her around? That's practically unheard of." 
That genuinely surprised Fleming, if only a little. "Find it rather astonishing that there are things you have not heard about." 
Fleming immediately regretted it when those words blurted out of his mouth. Thankfully, M3 was not in the leisurely mood to interpret his verbal mishap as a taunt. 
"A vast land has perished in her shadow. Millennia-worth of winters heed her beck and call. Yet she remains hungry." 
"It's the blood. We found other Nachzehrers. So many deaths are birthed upon this planet everyday. We have no desire to see another War Court appear without warning. But ... this child is obviously an exception. She has not been 'fed' because she respects every crew mate, messenger, and soldier who died in the frontiers. She could not bring herself to do it. In fact, she refuses to do it." 
"Then how did her power..." 
"'Though she did not consume the dead to strengthen herself, Death remains willing to assist her.' That wendigo friend of yours gave this assessment." 
"...Nezzsalem would be extremely moved if he were here." 
"But that also means the child is destined to take on burdens that shouldn't be hers." 
"I suppose this is the actual reason you recommended her to Endfield." 
"If Adelheid hopes to take upon a path of her choice, I believe Endfield Industries will be her best instructor." 
M3 was obviously taken aback. Fleming himself was also stunned by her reaction. He knew that M3 never expected him to give such a ... soft and compassionate answer. However, he also did not expect M3 to had judged him so poorly. It was a depressing realization for the merchant and consultant. 
"Well, Fleming ... perhaps you are kinder than I thought." 
Those words allowed Fleming's confidence to return. 
"And that is also your kindest evaluation of my character for all these years we've known each other, Miss M3." 
M3 sighed. It would seem she finally allowed herself to relax. "Now, how would you like Endfield to treat her?" 
"The usual," Fleming smiled from the bottom of his heart for the first time in this dialog. "Let her do what she wants, like a normal child. Let her live, get into trouble, grow up, and earn her keep. It would be wonderful if she gets to make a few friends and discover what she wants out of life..." 
"Treating her as your own?" 
"Hah. Me? My blood's too poor for her," Fleming also shifted his gaze to the window. Adelheid was already getting overwhelmed by other Endfield operators trying to start a conversation with her. 
"But before Talos-II forces humanity to the brink of extinction, before Death completely fashions her bloodied throne, and before the next Sovereign of the Nachzehrers is forced to manifest upon this planet ... she simply remains as a shy little Sarkaz girl."</>
